title.zh: 卷一百五十四 列傳第四十一: 洪福源 鄭鼎 李進 石抹按只 謁只里 鄭溫
title.en: Volume 154 Biographies 41: Hong Bok-won, Zheng Ding, Li Jin, Shi Moanzhi, Ye Zhili, Zheng Wen
title.raw: 卷一百五十四 列傳第四十一: 洪福源 鄭鼎 李進 石抹按只 謁只里 鄭溫 Volume 154 Biographies 41: Hong Bok-won, Zheng Ding, Li Jin, Shi Moanzhi, Ye Zhili, Zheng Wen

sentences.zh: 洪福源俊奇 君祥 萬

translations.literal: Hong Fuk-yeon; Junqi; Junxiang; Wan
translations.idiomatic: Hong Bok-won — with sub-biographies of Junqi, Junxiang, and Wan

sentences.zh: 洪福源，其先中國人，唐遣才子八人往教高麗，洪其一也。

translations.literal: Hong Fuk-yeon: his ancestors were men of China. In Tang times eight talented men were sent to instruct Goryeo; Hong was one of them.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Bok-won's forebears were Chinese. During the Tang, eight accomplished scholars were dispatched to instruct Goryeo, and Hong was one of them.

sentences.zh: 子孫世貴於三韓，名所居曰唐城。

translations.literal: Their descendants were eminent for generations in the Three Han, and they named their residence Tang City.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his line held high standing among the Three Han states of Korea, and they called their seat Tang City.

sentences.zh: 父大宣，以都領鎮麟州，福源為神騎都領，因家焉。

translations.literal: His father Dae Seon, as commander-in-chief, garrisoned Rin Prefecture; Fuk-yeon served as commander of the divine cavalry and therefore made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dae Seon held command at Rin Prefecture as a frontier commander; Fuk-yeon served as commander of the divine cavalry corps and settled his household there.

sentences.zh: 歲丙子，金源、契丹九萬餘衆竄入高麗。

translations.literal: In the year bingzi, more than ninety thousand troops of the Jin source and Khitan fled into Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingzi year, more than ninety thousand Jin and Khitan troops fled into Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 丁丑九月，奪江東城池據之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of dingchou they seized walled cities east of the River and occupied them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of dingchou they seized walled towns east of the Yalu and held them.

sentences.zh: 戊寅冬十二月，太祖命哈赤吉、扎剌將兵追討，大宣迎降，與哈赤吉等共擊之，降其元帥趙沖。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter in wuyin, Taizu ordered Hacheji and Zhala to lead troops in pursuit; Dae Seon came out to submit, joined Hacheji and the others in attacking them, and caused their commander Zhao Chong to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter in wuyin, Taizu ordered Hacheji and Zhala to lead troops in pursuit. Dae Seon came forward to submit, joined them in the attack, and brought their commander Zhao Chong to surrender.

sentences.zh: 壬午冬十月，又遣著古與等十二人窺覘納款虛實，還，遇害。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in renwu, twelve men including Zhuguyu were again sent to spy out whether their offer of submission was genuine; on their return they were killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter in renwu, twelve men including Zhuguyu were again sent to probe whether Goryeo's offer of submission was sincere; on their return they were murdered.

sentences.zh: 辛卯秋九月，太宗命將撒里荅討之，福源率先附州縣之民，與撒禮塔併力攻未附者，又與阿兒禿等進至王京。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn in xinmao, Taizong ordered the general Sarid to chastise them. Fuk-yeon took the lead in rallying the people of prefectures and counties that had submitted, joined Saritai in attacking those who had not submitted, and advanced with Arto and others to Wanggyeong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn in xinmao, Taizong ordered General Sarid to punish them. Fuk-yeon rallied the submitted prefectures and counties first, joined Saritai in pressing those still holding out, and advanced with Arto and others as far as the capital at Wanggyeong.

sentences.zh: 高麗王乃遣其弟懷安公請降，遂置王京及州縣達魯花赤七十二人以鎮之，師還。

translations.literal: The king of Goryeo then sent his younger brother, the Duke of Huai'an, to request surrender. Seventy-two darughachi were then placed in the capital and in prefectures and counties to garrison them, and the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Goryeo then sent his younger brother, the Duke of Huai'an, to sue for peace. Seventy-two darughachi were installed in the capital and in the prefectures and counties to hold them, and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 壬辰夏六月，高麗復叛，殺所置達魯花赤，悉驅國人入據江華島，福源招集北界四十餘城遺民以待。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer in renchen, Goryeo rebelled again, killed the darughachi that had been appointed, and drove all the people of the country to take refuge on Ganghwa Island. Fuk-yeon gathered the surviving populace of more than forty northern cities and waited.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer in renchen, Goryeo rebelled again, killed the appointed darughachi, and drove the whole population onto Ganghwa Island. Fuk-yeon gathered survivors from more than forty northern cities and held them in readiness.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，太宗復遣撒禮塔將兵來討，福源盡率所部合攻之，至王京處仁城，撒禮塔中流矢卒，其副帖哥引兵還，唯福源留屯。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn, Taizong again sent Saritai to lead troops to punish them. Fuk-yeon mustered all his forces to join the attack. When they reached the capital's Ch'inju City, Saritai was struck by an arrow and died; his deputy Tiege withdrew the army, and only Fuk-yeon remained encamped.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn, Taizong again sent Saritai with an army to chastise them. Fuk-yeon led his entire command to join the assault. At Ch'inju, a suburb of the capital, Saritai was struck by an arrow and died; his lieutenant Tiege withdrew, leaving only Fuk-yeon to hold the camp.

sentences.zh: 癸巳冬十月，高麗悉衆來攻西京，屠其民，劫大宣以東。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in guisi, Goryeo mustered its entire force to attack Sŏgyŏng, slaughtered its people, and carried Dae Seon off eastward.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter in guisi, Goryeo threw its full strength against the Western Capital, massacred its people, and carried Dae Seon off to the east.

sentences.zh: 福源遂盡以所招集北界之衆來歸，處於遼陽、瀋陽之間，帝嘉其忠。

translations.literal: Fuk-yeon then brought all the people he had gathered on the northern frontier to submit; they were settled between Liaoyang and Shenyang. The emperor praised his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Fuk-yeon then led all the people he had gathered on the northern frontier back to allegiance and settled them between Liaoyang and Shenyang. The emperor commended his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 甲午夏五月，特賜金符，為管領歸附高麗軍民長官，仍令招討本國未附人民。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer in jiawu, he was specially granted a gold tally and appointed chief official in charge of Goryeo troops and people who had submitted, and was still ordered to recruit the unsubmitted people of his native country.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer in jiawu, he was specially granted a gold tally and made chief officer over the Goryeo troops and people who had submitted, with orders still to win over those in his homeland who had not yet come in.

sentences.zh: 又降旨諭高麗之民，有執王及元搆難之人來朝者，與洪福源同於東京居之，優加恩禮擢用，若大兵既加，拒者死，降者生，其降民令福源統之。

translations.literal: An edict was also issued instructing the people of Goryeo: whoever came to court having seized the king or men who had caused trouble for the Yuan would dwell at Dongjing together with Hong Fuk-yeon, receive favor and promotion; once great armies arrived, those who resisted would die and those who surrendered would live, and the surrendered populace was to be placed under Fuk-yeon's command.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict addressed the people of Goryeo: whoever came to court having seized the king or those who had stirred trouble against the Yuan would live at Dongjing with Hong Fuk-yeon and receive favor and promotion; when the great armies came, resisters would die and submitters would live, and all who surrendered were to be placed under Fuk-yeon's command.

sentences.zh: 乙未，帝命唐古拔都兒與福源進討，攻拔龍崗、咸從二縣，鳳、海、洞三州山城及慈州，又拔金山、歸、信、昌、朔州。

translations.literal: In yiwei, the emperor ordered Tangqubadur and Fuk-yeon to advance and chastise. They captured the two counties of Longgang and Xiancong, the mountain fortresses of the three prefectures Feng, Hai, and Dong, and Cizhou; they also took Jinshan and the prefectures Gui, Xin, Chang, and Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: In yiwei, the emperor ordered Tangqubadur and Fuk-yeon to advance in punishment. They took the counties of Longgang and Xiancong, the mountain strongholds of Feng, Hai, and Dong prefectures, and Cizhou, and also captured Jinshan and the prefectures of Gui, Xin, Chang, and Shuo.

sentences.zh: 己亥春二月，入朝，賜以鎧甲弓矢，及金織文段、金銀器、金鞍勒等。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring in jihai, he came to court and was given armor, bow and arrows, gold-woven brocade, gold and silver vessels, gold saddle and bridle, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring in jihai he came to court and was granted armor, bow and arrows, gold-woven brocades, gold and silver vessels, a gold saddle and bridle, and the like.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，定宗命阿母罕將兵與福源共拔威州平虜城。

translations.literal: In yisi, Emperor Dingzong ordered Amuhan to lead troops with Fuk-yeon jointly to take Weizhou's Pinglu Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: In yisi, Emperor Dingzong ordered Amuhan to lead troops with Fuk-yeon to capture the Pinglu fortress at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，憲宗即位，改授虎符，仍為前後歸附高麗軍民長官。

translations.literal: In xinhai, when Emperor Xianzong acceded, he was given a tiger tally in replacement and remained chief official of Goryeo troops and people who had submitted earlier and later.
translations.idiomatic: In xinhai, when Emperor Xianzong took the throne, he was reissued a tiger tally and retained his post as chief officer over all Goryeo troops and people who had submitted, past and present.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，從諸王耶虎攻禾山、東州、春州、三角山、楊根、天龍等城，拔之。

translations.literal: In guichou, he followed Princely Lord Yehu to attack the cities of Heshan, Dongzhou, Chunzhou, Sanjiaoshan, Yanggen, Tianlong, and others, and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: In guichou he followed Prince Yehu in attacks on Heshan, Dongzhou, Chunzhou, Sanjiaoshan, Yanggen, Tianlong, and other cities, and took them all.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，與扎剌台合兵攻光州、安城、忠州、玄風、珍原、甲向、玉果等城，又拔之。

translations.literal: In jiayin, he united forces with Zhalatai to attack the cities of Guangzhou, Ancheng, Zhongzhou, Xuanfeng, Zhenyuan, Jiaxiang, Yuguo, and others, and again captured them.
translations.idiomatic: In jiayin he joined Zhalatai to assault Guangzhou, Ancheng, Zhongzhou, Xuanfeng, Zhenyuan, Jiaxiang, Yuguo, and other cities, and captured them as well.

sentences.zh: 戊午，福源遣其子茶丘從扎剌台軍，會高麗族子王綧入質，陰欲併統本國歸順人民，譖福源于帝，遂見殺，年五十三。

translations.literal: In wuwu, Fuk-yeon sent his son Ch'aek'u to follow Zhalatai's army. A clansman of Goryeo, Wang Wan, who had come as hostage, secretly wished to annex control of all the submitted people of the country, slandered Fuk-yeon to the emperor, and he was thereupon put to death at age fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In wuwu, Fuk-yeon sent his son Ch'aek'u to serve under Zhalatai. Wang Wan, a Goryeo clansman who had come as a hostage, secretly sought to bring all who had submitted in his homeland under his own control, slandered Fuk-yeon to the emperor, and Fuk-yeon was put to death at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 後贈嘉議大夫、瀋陽侯，諡忠憲。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously enfeoffed as Counselor of the Empire and Marquis of Shenyang, with the posthumous title Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was posthumously granted the title Counselor of the Empire and enfeoffed as Marquis of Shenyang, with the posthumous epithet Loyal and Just.

sentences.zh: 子七人，俊奇、君祥最知名。

translations.literal: He had seven sons; Junqi and Junxiang were the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons; Junqi and Junxiang were the best known.

sentences.zh: 俊奇小字茶丘，福源第二子也。

translations.literal: Junqi's childhood name was Ch'aek'u; he was Fuk-yeon's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Junqi, whose childhood name was Ch'aek'u, was Fuk-yeon's second son.

sentences.zh: 幼從軍，以驍勇受知，世祖嘗以小字呼之。

translations.literal: From youth he followed the armies; for his valor he won notice, and Shizu would call him by his childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he followed the campaigns; his daring won him notice, and Kublai would address him by his childhood name.

sentences.zh: 中統二年秋，茶丘雪父冤，世祖憫之，詔諭之曰：「汝父方加寵用，誤絓刑章，故於已廢之中，庸沛維新之澤。

translations.literal: In autumn of the second year of Zhongtong, Ch'aek'u vindicated his father's injustice. Shizu took pity on him and issued an edict saying: "Your father was just receiving increased favor when he was mistakenly caught in penal statutes; therefore, amid what had been abolished, we pour forth the grace of renewal in full measure.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the second year of Zhongtong, Ch'aek'u cleared his father's name. Kublai took pity on him and issued an edict: "Your father had just been raised to greater favor when he was caught by mistake in the penal code; therefore, though his line had been cut off, we now pour out the full measure of renewal upon you.

sentences.zh: 可就帶元降虎符，襲父職，管領歸附高麗軍民緫管。」

translations.literal: You may forthwith wear the tiger tally for surrendered Yuan troops, inherit your father's post, and serve as commissioner-general of submitted Goryeo troops and people."
translations.idiomatic: You may now wear the tiger tally for surrendered Yuan troops, inherit your father's office, and serve as commissioner-general over the submitted Goryeo troops and people."

sentences.zh: 至元六年，高麗權臣林衍叛。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan, the powerful minister of Goryeo Lin Yan rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan, Lin Yan, a powerful minister of Goryeo, rebelled.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，詔以其軍三千從國王頭輦哥討平之，遷江華島所有臣民，復歸王京。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter an edict ordered that with three thousand of his troops he follow the Goryeo king Tolichi in suppressing the rebellion; the subjects on Ganghwa Island were moved back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter an edict ordered him to take three thousand of his troops and follow the Goryeo king Tolichi to put down the rebellion; all subjects on Ganghwa Island were moved back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十二月，帝命茶丘率兵往鳳州等處，立屯田緫管府。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the emperor ordered Ch'aek'u to lead troops to Fengzhou and other places and establish an agricultural colony commissioner's office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the emperor ordered Ch'aek'u to lead troops to Fengzhou and other districts and establish an agricultural colony commissioner's office.

sentences.zh: 八年二月，入朝，賜鈔百緡。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year he came to court and was given one hundred strings of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year he came to court and was granted one hundred strings of paper money.

sentences.zh: 林衍餘黨裴仲孫等，立高麗王禃親屬承化侯為王，引三別抄軍據珍島以叛。

translations.literal: Lin Yan's remnant followers Pei Zhongsun and others set up as king Chengdehou, a relative of King Ch'ŏ of Goryeo, and led the Three Separate Corps to occupy Jin Island in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yan's remnant followers, Pei Zhongsun and others, set up the Marquis of Chenghua, a kinsman of King Ch'ŏ of Goryeo, as king and led the Three Separate Corps to hold Jin Island in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 五月，茶丘奉旨，偕經略使欣都進兵討之，破其軍，殺承化侯，其黨金通精率餘衆走耽羅。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Ch'aek'u received the imperial order and, together with pacification commissioner Xindu, advanced to chastise them, routed their army, and killed Chengdehou. Their partisan Jintongjing led the remainder to flee to Tamna.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Ch'aek'u received the imperial order and, with Pacification Commissioner Xindu, advanced to punish them, routed their army, and killed the Marquis of Chenghua. Their partisan Jintongjing led the survivors to flee to Tamna.

sentences.zh: 帝遣侍衛親軍千戶王岑，與茶丘議征取之策，茶丘表陳：「通精之黨，多在王京，可使招之，招而不從，擊之未晚。

translations.literal: The emperor sent thousand-household Wang Cen of the imperial guard to discuss with Ch'aek'u strategy for taking them. Ch'aek'u memorialized: "The followers of Tongjing are mostly in the capital; they may be induced to surrender — if they do not surrender when summoned, it will not be too late to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Wang Cen, a thousand-household of the imperial guard, to discuss strategy with Ch'aek'u. Ch'aek'u memorialized: "Most of Tongjing's followers are in the capital; they can be summoned to surrender, and if they refuse, it will not be too late to strike.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his plan.

sentences.zh: 俄奉旨往羅州道監造戰船，且招降耽羅，茶丘得通精之姪金永等七人，俾招之，通精不從，留金永，餘盡殺之。

translations.literal: Before long he received orders to go to the Luozhou circuit to supervise the building of warships and also to induce Tamna to surrender. Ch'aek'u obtained Tongjing's nephew Kim Yong and seven others, had them summon him; Tongjing refused, so Kim Yong was detained and the rest were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he received orders to go to the Luozhou circuit to supervise construction of warships and also to win Tamna's submission. Ch'aek'u obtained Tongjing's nephew Kim Yong and six others, sent them to summon him; Tongjing refused, so Kim Yong was kept and the rest were all executed.

sentences.zh: 十年，詔茶丘與欣都率兵渡海，擊破耽羅，獲通精，殺之，悉免其脅從者，高麗始平。

translations.literal: In the tenth year an edict ordered Ch'aek'u and Xindu to lead troops across the sea, defeated Tamna, captured Tongjing and executed him, and entirely spared those who had been coerced to follow — only then was Goryeo pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year an edict ordered Ch'aek'u and Xindu to lead troops across the sea, broke Tamna, captured Tongjing and executed him, and spared all who had been forced to follow him; only then was Goryeo fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 十一年，又命監造戰船，經營日本國事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was again ordered to supervise building warships and to manage affairs toward Japan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was again ordered to supervise construction of warships and to manage affairs relating to Japan.

sentences.zh: 三月，授昭勇大將軍、安撫使，高麗軍民緫管如故。

translations.literal: In the third month he was appointed General of Manifest Valor and Pacification Commissioner, his post as commissioner-general of Goryeo troops and people remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was appointed General of Manifest Valor and Pacification Commissioner, retaining his post as commissioner-general over Goryeo troops and people.

sentences.zh: 己卯，命茶丘提點高麗農事。

translations.literal: In jimao the emperor ordered Ch'aek'u to oversee Goryeo agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In the jimao year the emperor ordered Ch'aek'u to oversee agricultural affairs in Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 八月，授東征右副都元帥，與都元帥忽敦等領舟師二萬，渡海征日本，拔對馬、一岐、宜蠻等島。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was appointed deputy supreme commander of the Eastern Expedition on the right; with the supreme commander Hudun and others he led a fleet of twenty thousand, crossed the sea to campaign against Japan, and took the islands of Tsushima, Iki, and Ima.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was made deputy supreme commander of the Eastern Expedition on the right; with Supreme Commander Hudun and others he led a fleet of twenty thousand, crossed the sea against Japan, and took Tsushima, Iki, Ima, and other islands.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，授鎮國上將軍、東征都元帥，鎮高麗。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year he was appointed General Who Stabilizes the Realm and supreme commander of the Eastern Expedition, stationed in Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourteenth year he was appointed General Who Stabilizes the Realm and supreme commander of the Eastern Expedition, with his base in Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 二月，率蒙古、高麗、女直、漢軍，從丞相伯顏北征叛臣只魯瓦歹等。

translations.literal: In the second month he led Mongol, Goryeo, Jurchen, and Han troops following the chancellor Bayan north to campaign against the rebel minister Jiluwadai and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he led Mongol, Goryeo, Jurchen, and Han troops under Chancellor Bayan on the northern campaign against the rebel minister Jiluwadai and others.

sentences.zh: 四月，至脫剌河，猝與賊遇，茶丘突陣無前，伯顏以其勇聞，賜白金五十兩、金鞍勒、弓矢。

translations.literal: In the fourth month when they reached the Tuoluo River they suddenly encountered the rebels. Ch'aek'u charged the formation without peer. Bayan had his courage reported and bestowed fifty taels of white gold, a gold saddle and bridle, and bow and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, when they reached the Tuoluo River, they suddenly met the rebels. Ch'aek'u charged the enemy line without equal. Bayan reported his valor to the throne, and he was granted fifty taels of white gold, a gold saddle and bridle, and bow and arrows.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授龍虎衛上將軍、征東行省右丞。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Tiger-Dragon Guard General and right vice-censor of the Eastern Campaign Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Tiger-Dragon Guard General and right vice-censor of the Eastern Campaign Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十八年，與右丞欣都將舟師四萬，由高麗金州合浦以進，時右丞范文虎等將兵十萬，由慶元、定海等處渡海，期至日本一岐、平戶等島合兵登岸，兵未交，秋八月，風壞舟而還。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he and right vice-censor Xindu led a fleet of forty thousand from Hap'p'o at Goryeo's Kim Province. At that time right vice-censor Fan Wenhu and others led one hundred thousand troops across the sea from Qingyuan and Dinghai, with a rendezvous to land on Japan's Iki and Hirado islands — but before battle was joined, in the eighth month of autumn wind wrecked the boats and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he and Vice-Censor Xindu led a fleet of forty thousand from Hap'p'o in Goryeo's Kim Province. At the same time Vice-Censor Fan Wenhu and others led one hundred thousand troops across the sea from Qingyuan and Dinghai, with a rendezvous to land on Iki and Hirado in Japan — but before battle was joined, in the eighth month of autumn storms wrecked the ships and the fleets returned.

sentences.zh: 十九年十月，命茶丘於平灤黑堝兒監造戰船七百艘，以圖後舉。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the nineteenth year the emperor ordered Ch'aek'u at Pingluan Heigun'er to supervise construction of seven hundred warships for a future effort.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the nineteenth year the emperor ordered Ch'aek'u to supervise construction of seven hundred warships at Pingluan Heigun'er for a future campaign.

sentences.zh: 二十一年十一月，復授征東行省右丞。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the twenty-first year he was again appointed right vice-censor of the Eastern Campaign Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the twenty-first year he was again appointed right vice-censor of the Eastern Campaign Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，命往江浙等處遣漢人復業。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was ordered to go to Jiang-Zhe and other circuits to send Han people back to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was ordered to Jiang-Zhe and other circuits to restore Han people to their former occupations.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，乃顏叛，車駕親征，賜以翎根甲、寶刀，命率高麗、女直、漢軍扈從。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Nayan rebelled; the imperial carriage personally campaigned. He was given feather-root armor and a precious sword and ordered to lead Goryeo, Jurchen, and Han troops in escort.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year Nayan rebelled and the emperor campaigned in person. Ch'aek'u was granted feather-root armor and a precious sword and ordered to lead Goryeo, Jurchen, and Han troops in the imperial escort.

sentences.zh: 猝遇乃顏騎兵萬餘，時茶丘兵不滿三千，衆有懼色，茶丘夜令軍中，多裂裳帛為旗幟，斷馬尾為旄，掩暎林木，張設疑兵，乃顏兵大驚，以為官兵大至，遂降。

translations.literal: They suddenly met more than ten thousand of Nayan's cavalry. At the time Ch'aek'u's troops numbered fewer than three thousand and the men showed fear. Ch'aek'u ordered the army by night to tear many robes into banners and cut horses' tails for pennons, setting them among the trees to make a display of suspicious forces. Nayan's troops were greatly alarmed, thinking a large imperial army had arrived, and thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: They suddenly encountered more than ten thousand of Nayan's horsemen. Ch'aek'u had fewer than three thousand troops and his men showed fear. That night he ordered the army to tear many garments into banners and cut horses' tails for pennons, planting them among the trees as a ruse. Nayan's troops were thrown into panic, believing a great imperial force had arrived, and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，厚加旌賞，凱還，授遼陽等處行尚書省右丞。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of this he richly rewarded him. On the triumphant return he was appointed right vice-minister of the Branch Secretariat of Liaoyang and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he richly rewarded him. On the triumphant return he was appointed right vice-minister of the Branch Secretariat for Liaoyang and adjacent regions.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，以疾辭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he resigned on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 叛王哈丹等竄入高麗，侵撓其國西京，距遼陽二千里皆騷動，中書省特起茶丘鎮遼左，帝遣闍里台孛羅兒賜以金字圓符，命茶丘以便宜行事。

translations.literal: The rebel prince Hadan and others fled into Goryeo and harassed that country's Western Capital; within two thousand li of Liaoyang there was disturbance everywhere. The Secretariat specially raised Ch'aek'u to pacify eastern Liaoning. The emperor sent Qielitai Boluo'er with a round gold-character tally ordering Ch'aek'u to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel prince Hadan and others fled into Goryeo and raided its Western Capital; for two thousand li around Liaoyang the region was in turmoil. The Secretariat specially recalled Ch'aek'u to pacify eastern Liaoning. The emperor sent Qielitai Boluo'er with a round gold-character tally empowering Ch'aek'u to act at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，以疾卒，年四十八。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died of illness at age forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he died of illness at the age of forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子四人，長曰萬。

translations.literal: He had four sons; the eldest was called Wan.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons; the eldest was named Wan.

sentences.zh: 君祥小字雙叔，福源第五子也。

translations.literal: Junxiang's childhood name was Shuangshu; he was Fuk-yeon's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Junxiang, whose childhood name was Shuangshu, was Fuk-yeon's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 年十四，隨兄茶丘見世祖于上京，帝悅，命劉秉忠相之，秉忠曰：「是兒目視不凡，後必以功名顯，但當致力于學耳。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he followed his elder brother Ch'aek'u to see Shizu at Shangdu. The emperor was pleased, ordered Liu Bingzhong to look at his physiognomy; Bingzhong said, "This boy's gaze is uncommon — he will later distinguish himself by merit and fame, but he must devote himself to learning.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he accompanied his elder brother Ch'aek'u to audience with Kublai at Shangdu. The emperor was pleased and ordered Liu Bingzhong to read his physiognomy. Bingzhong said, "This boy's gaze is uncommon — he will later win fame through achievement, but he must devote himself to learning.

sentences.zh: 」令選師儒誨之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that learned teachers be chosen to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that learned teachers be chosen to instruct him.

sentences.zh: 至元三年，籍高麗民三百人為兵，令君祥統之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiyuan three hundred Goryeo households were registered as troops and Junxiang was ordered to command them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhiyuan three hundred Goryeo households were registered as troops and placed under Junxiang's command.

sentences.zh: 從禿花禿烈、伯顏等軍，築萬壽山，復從開通州運河。

translations.literal: He followed the armies of Tuohuatuolie, Bayan, and others in building the Longevity Hill and again worked on the Tongzhou Canal.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Tuohuatuolie, Bayan, and others in building Longevity Hill and later on the Tongzhou Canal.

sentences.zh: 帝親諭之曰：「爾守志忠勤，朕所知也。

translations.literal: The emperor personally addressed him: "You have kept your resolve loyal and diligent — this I know of you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor addressed him personally: "Your steadfast loyalty and diligence are known to me.

sentences.zh: 」帝嘗坐便殿，閱江南、海東輿地圖，欲召知者詢其險易，左丞相伯顏、樞密副使合達，以君祥應旨，奏對詳明，帝悅，酌以巨觥。

translations.literal: " Once when the emperor sat in the informal hall examining maps of Jiangnan and the eastern sea, wishing to summon someone knowledgeable to inquire about the terrain's advantages and difficulties, Left Chancellor Bayan and Vice Censor-in-Chief Heda recommended Junxiang to answer the summons. His reply was detailed and clear; the emperor was pleased and poured him a large cup.
translations.idiomatic: " Once, seated in the informal hall, the emperor studied maps of Jiangnan and the eastern sea and wished to summon someone who knew the terrain to ask about its strengths and weaknesses. Left Chancellor Bayan and Vice Censor-in-Chief Heda recommended Junxiang. His answers were detailed and clear; the emperor was pleased and poured him a great cup of wine.

sentences.zh: 顧謂伯顏曰：「是兒，遠大器也。」

translations.literal: Turning to Bayan he said, "This boy is a vessel of far-reaching capacity."
translations.idiomatic: Turning to Bayan he said, "This boy is a vessel of great promise."

sentences.zh: 六年，林衍叛，從頭輦哥征之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Lin Yan rebelled; he followed Tolichi in the punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when Lin Yan rebelled, he followed Tolichi on the punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 八年，戍河南。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he garrisoned Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was posted to garrison Henan.

sentences.zh: 九年，掠淮西，破其大凹城。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he raided west of the Huai and captured their great Ao walled city.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he raided west of the Huai and captured the great walled city of Da'ao.

sentences.zh: 十年，從元帥孛魯罕襲淮東之射陽湖，俘其男女牛馬。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he followed Marshal Boluhan in a raid on the Sheyang Lake east of the Huai and captured men, women, oxen, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he followed Marshal Boluhan in a raid on Sheyang Lake east of the Huai and took captives, cattle, and horses.

sentences.zh: 十一年，入朝。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he came to court.

sentences.zh: 帝命伯顏伐宋，朝議以宋之兵力多聚兩淮，聞我欲渡江，彼必移師拒守，遂命右衛指揮使禿滿歹，率輕銳二萬攻淮安，以牽制之，君祥以蒙古漢軍都鎮撫從行。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Bayan to attack Song. Court discussion held that Song's main forces were massed on both sides of the Huai; hearing that we intended to cross the Yangzi they would certainly shift troops to block us. Therefore Right Guard Commander Tuomandai was ordered to lead twenty thousand light, elite troops to attack Huai'an as a diversion; Junxiang accompanied as commander-in-chief of Mongol and Han troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Bayan to attack Song. Court opinion held that Song's main strength was massed on both Huai fronts and that, hearing of our plan to cross the Yangzi, they would shift troops to block us. Right Guard Commander Tuomandai was therefore ordered to lead twenty thousand light, elite troops against Huai'an as a diversion; Junxiang accompanied him as commander-in-chief of Mongol and Han forces.

sentences.zh: 後伯顏既渡江，帝命禿滿歹還軍蕭縣。

translations.literal: After Bayan had crossed the Yangzi the emperor ordered Tuomandai to withdraw the army to Xiao County.
translations.idiomatic: After Bayan had crossed the Yangzi, the emperor ordered Tuomandai to withdraw his force to Xiao County.

sentences.zh: 時君祥奉使伯顏軍中，宋黃州制置使陳奕降，其子知漣水軍，伯顏遣三十騎往招之，因令君祥入奏，帝曰：「卿可急還，陳知府降，即偕來也。

translations.literal: At this time Junxiang was on mission in Bayan's army. Song's Huangzhou commissioner Chen Yi surrendered; his son commanded the Lianshui army. Bayan sent thirty horsemen to summon him and also had Junxiang enter court with a memorial. The emperor said, "You may return posthaste — when Prefect Chen surrenders, bring him together with you.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Junxiang was on mission in Bayan's army. Song's Huangzhou commissioner Chen Yi surrendered; his son held command at Lianshui. Bayan sent thirty horsemen to summon them and had Junxiang report to court. The emperor said, "Return at once — when Prefect Chen surrenders, bring him with you.

sentences.zh: 」及與俱入朝，宴勞甚厚。

translations.literal: " When they entered court together they were banqueted and rewarded with great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: " When they entered court together, they were banqueted and rewarded with exceptional generosity.

sentences.zh: 從元帥孛魯罕攻清河，拔之。

translations.literal: He followed Marshal Boluhan in attacking Qinghe and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Marshal Boluhan in the attack on Qinghe and captured it.

sentences.zh: 海州安撫丁順約降，孛魯罕令君祥以聞，時伯顏方朝上京，見君祥，甚喜，遂從南伐。

translations.literal: The Haizhou pacification commissioner Ding Shun agreed to surrender; Boluhan had Junxiang report this. At the time Bayan was on his way to court at Shangdu; seeing Junxiang he was very pleased and thereupon followed the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Haizhou Pacification Commissioner Ding Shun agreed to surrender; Boluhan had Junxiang report this. Bayan was then on his way to audience at Shangdu; delighted to see Junxiang, he took him south on the campaign.

sentences.zh: 伯顏克淮安，至揚州，分兵攻淮西。

translations.literal: Bayan took Huai'an and reached Yangzhou; he divided troops to attack west of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan captured Huai'an and advanced to Yangzhou, then divided his forces to strike west of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 宋制置夏貴遣牛都統以書抵伯顏曰：「諺云：殺人一萬，自損三千。

translations.literal: Song commissioner Xia Gui sent Commander Niu with a letter to Bayan saying: "The proverb runs: 'Slay ten thousand of the enemy and lose three thousand of your own.'
translations.idiomatic: Song commissioner Xia Gui sent Commander Niu with a letter to Bayan: "The proverb says, 'Slay ten thousand of the enemy and lose three thousand of your own.'

sentences.zh: 願勿廢國力，攻奪邊城，若行在歸附，邊城焉往。

translations.literal: I pray you do not waste the state's strength attacking border towns — if the traveling palace submits, what becomes of the border towns.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you not to exhaust the state's strength seizing border towns — if the court submits, of what use are the border towns.

sentences.zh: 」伯顏遣君祥以牛都統入見，留三日，還軍中。

translations.literal: Bayan sent Junxiang to bring Commander Niu in audience; Junxiang stayed three days and returned to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan sent Junxiang to escort Commander Niu to audience; after three days Junxiang returned to the army.

sentences.zh: 仍傳旨諭伯顏曰：「事難遙度，宜臨機審圖之。

translations.literal: He still transmitted an edict to Bayan: "Matters are hard to judge from afar — you should weigh them on the spot."
translations.idiomatic: He also conveyed an edict to Bayan: "Affairs are hard to judge from a distance — you should weigh them on the spot."

sentences.zh: 」伯顏師次鎮江，諜報有宋洪都統者，為都督府將，伯顏謂君祥曰：「汝同姓，可往招致也。

translations.literal: " Bayan's army halted at Zhenjiang. Scouts reported a Song Commander Hong of the metropolitan guard; Bayan said to Junxiang, "You share his surname — you may go to win him over.
translations.idiomatic: " Bayan's army halted at Zhenjiang. Scouts reported a Song commander named Hong in the metropolitan guard corps. Bayan said to Junxiang, "You share his surname — go and win him over.

sentences.zh: 」洪都統即欣然來見，君祥因厚遇之。

translations.literal: " Commander Hong came gladly to see him, and Junxiang treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: " Commander Hong came willingly to meet him, and Junxiang treated him with great courtesy.

sentences.zh: 師進，次臨平山，距臨安五十里，洪都統來報曰：「宋丞相陳宜中、殿帥張世傑皆已逃去，惟三宮未行，宜早定計，以活生民。

translations.literal: When the army advanced and halted at Linping Hill, fifty li from Lin'an, Commander Hong came to report: "Song chancellor Chen Yizhong and palace commander Zhang Shijie have both fled; only the three inner palaces have not departed — you should settle plans early to spare the people.
translations.idiomatic: As the army advanced and halted at Linping Hill, fifty li from Lin'an, Commander Hong came with word: "Song chancellor Chen Yizhong and palace commander Zhang Shijie have both fled; only the three palaces have not yet departed — settle your plans soon to spare the people.

sentences.zh: 」伯顏遂令洪都統護宋三宮，令君祥隨之。

translations.literal: " Bayan thereupon had Commander Hong escort the three palaces of Song and ordered Junxiang to follow.
translations.idiomatic: " Bayan then had Commander Hong escort the three Song palaces and ordered Junxiang to accompany them.

sentences.zh: 宋降，陞武略將軍、中衛親軍千戶。

translations.literal: When Song surrendered, he was promoted to Martial Stratagem General and thousand-household of the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Song surrendered, he was promoted to Martial Stratagem General and thousand-household of the Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 十五年，命簽江南民兵。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was ordered to muster Jiangnan militia.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was ordered to register Jiangnan militia.

sentences.zh: 還，陞明威將軍、中衛親軍副都指揮使。

translations.literal: On return he was promoted to Majestic Wei General and deputy commander of the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was promoted to Majestic Wei General and deputy commander of the Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 十七年，進昭勇大將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was advanced to General of Manifest Valor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was advanced to General of Manifest Valor.

sentences.zh: 十九年，授樞密院判官。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed a vice minister of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was appointed vice minister of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，轉昭武大將軍、同僉樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was transferred to Majestic Wu General and associate vice minister of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was transferred to Majestic Wu General and associate vice minister of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，乃顏叛，從世祖親征。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Nayan rebelled; he followed Shizu on the personal campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, when Nayan rebelled, he followed Kublai on the personal campaign.

sentences.zh: 每駐蹕，君祥輒以兵車外環為營衛，布置嚴密，帝嘉之。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor halted his march Junxiang would ring the camp with war wagons for protection, arranging defenses tightly; the emperor commended this.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor halted, Junxiang ringed the camp with war wagons as an outer guard, arranging defenses with great care; the emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 凱還，加輔國上將軍。

translations.literal: On the triumphant return he was additionally made Assistant-to-the-State General.
translations.idiomatic: On the triumphant return he was additionally made Assistant-to-the-State General.

sentences.zh: 類次車駕起居，為東征錄。

translations.literal: He compiled by category the imperial residence records into an Eastern Campaign Record.
translations.idiomatic: He arranged the imperial residence records by category into a Record of the Eastern Campaign.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，授遼陽行省右丞，用樞密院留，復居舊職。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed right vice-censor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat; retained at the Bureau of Military Affairs, he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed right vice-censor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, but was retained by the Bureau of Military Affairs and resumed his former post.

sentences.zh: 俄加集賢大學士，依舊同僉樞密院事。

translations.literal: Shortly he was additionally made Academician-Expositor of the Hall of Gathered Worthies while retaining his associate vice ministership.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was additionally made Academician-Expositor of the Hall of Gathered Worthies while retaining his associate vice ministership.

sentences.zh: 議者欲自東南海口辛橋開河合灤河，運糧至上都，奉旨與中書右丞阿里相其利害，還，極言不便，罷之。

translations.literal: Discussants wished to open a canal from Xinqiao on the eastern-southern sea mouth to join the Luan River and transport grain to Shangdu; by imperial order he and Right Vice-Censor Ali examined the advantages and disadvantages; on return he strongly argued it was impracticable and the plan was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed opening a canal from Xinqiao at the southeastern sea mouth to join the Luan River and ship grain to Shangdu; by imperial order he and Right Vice-Censor Ali surveyed the advantages and drawbacks. On his return he argued strongly against the plan and it was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 復奉使高麗，還，改僉書樞密院事。

translations.literal: Again he was sent on mission to Goryeo; on return he was changed to secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was again sent on mission to Goryeo; on his return he was appointed secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 成宗即位，詔裁減久任官，知樞密院暗伯等奏：「君祥在樞密十六年，最為久者。

translations.literal: When Chengzong acceded, an edict ordered reduction of officials long in one post. The Bureau of Military Affairs director Anbo and others memorialized: "Junxiang has been at the Bureau of Military Affairs sixteen years — the longest of any."
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong took the throne, an edict called for trimming officials who had held the same post too long. Director Anbo of the Bureau of Military Affairs and others memorialized: "Junxiang has served at the Bureau of Military Affairs for sixteen years — longer than anyone else."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「君祥始終一心，可勿遷也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Junxiang has been single-minded from first to last — he need not be transferred."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Junxiang has been steadfast throughout — let him remain where he is."

sentences.zh: 」大德二年，詔使高麗，臺臣劾君祥以他事，中道追回，已而事罷。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dade an edict sent him on mission to Goryeo. Censorate officials impeached Junxiang on another matter; he was recalled en route, and before long the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dade an edict sent him on mission to Goryeo. Censorate officials impeached him on another charge; he was recalled midway, and the matter was soon dropped.

sentences.zh: 三年，奉使江浙，問民間疾苦。

translations.literal: In the third year he was sent on mission to Jiang-Zhe to inquire into the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was sent to Jiang-Zhe on mission to inquire into the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 使還，退居昌平之皇華山，絕口不論時事者五年。

translations.literal: When the mission returned he retired to Huanghua Mountain in Changping and for five years never spoke of current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he retired to Huanghua Mountain in Changping and for five years would not speak of public affairs.

sentences.zh: 大德九年，擢司農，俄拜中書右丞。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dade he was promoted to Minister of Agriculture and shortly appointed right vice-censor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Dade he was promoted to Minister of Agriculture and soon appointed right vice-censor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十年春，改江浙行省右丞。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year he was changed to right vice-censor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the tenth year he was transferred to right vice-censor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 秋，改遼陽右丞，請於朝：宜新省治，增巡兵，設儒學提舉官、都鎮撫等員，以興文化，修武備。

translations.literal: In autumn he was changed to right vice-censor of Liaoyang and petitioned the court: the provincial seat should be renewed, patrol troops increased, and posts such as Confucian learning commissioner and commander-in-chief established to promote culture and strengthen military preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn he was transferred to right vice-censor of Liaoyang and petitioned the court to rebuild the provincial seat, increase patrol troops, and establish posts such as Confucian learning commissioner and commander-in-chief to promote culture and strengthen defenses.

sentences.zh: 事未成，會武宗即位，徵為同知樞密院事，進榮祿大夫、平章政事，商議遼陽等處行中書省事，改遼陽行省平章政事，俄改商議行省事。

translations.literal: Before the matter was accomplished, Wuzong acceded. He was summoned as associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and chief councilor, deliberated over Branch Secretariat affairs for Liaoyang and elsewhere, was changed to chief councilor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, and shortly changed to deliberating chief councilor of the branch secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before his plans could be carried out, Wuzong took the throne. He was summoned as associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and chief councilor, assigned to deliberate Branch Secretariat affairs for Liaoyang, made chief councilor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, and soon transferred to deliberating chief councilor of the branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至大二年卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Zhida.

sentences.zh: 子邁，奉訓大夫、同知開元緫管府事。

translations.literal: His son Mai was Instructor Grand Master and associate director of the Kaiyuan Commissioner's Office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mai held the rank Instructor Grand Master and served as associate director of the Kaiyuan Commissioner's Office.

sentences.zh: 萬小字重喜。

translations.literal: Wan's childhood name was Chongxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wan, whose childhood name was Chongxi.

sentences.zh: 至元十三年，入宿衛。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan he entered the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan he entered the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 十八年，襲職，為懷遠大將軍、安撫使、高麗軍民緫管，仍佩父茶丘所佩虎符。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he inherited the post, becoming General of Cherished Distance, Pacification Commissioner, and commissioner-general of Goryeo troops and people, still wearing the tiger tally his father Ch'aek'u had worn.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he inherited his father's office as General of Cherished Distance, Pacification Commissioner, and commissioner-general over Goryeo troops and people, still wearing the tiger tally his father Ch'aek'u had carried.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，乃顏叛，率兵征之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Nayan rebelled; he led troops to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, when Nayan rebelled, he led troops against him.

sentences.zh: 六月，至撒里禿魯之地，同都萬戶闍里鐵木兒，與乃顏將黃海戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, when they reached Saritulu, together with commander-in-chief Qielitie'er he fought Nayan's general Huang Hai and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, reaching Saritulu, he joined Commander-in-Chief Qielitie'er in battle against Nayan's general Huang Hai and routed him completely.

sentences.zh: 又從世祖與塔不台戰，又敗之。

translations.literal: He again followed Shizu in battle with Tabutai and again defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Kublai against Tabutai and defeated him once more.

sentences.zh: 是月，至乃顏之地，奉旨留蒙古、女直、漢軍鎮哈剌河。

translations.literal: That month, when they reached Nayan's territory, by imperial order he left Mongol, Jurchen, and Han troops to garrison the Hala River.
translations.idiomatic: That month, on reaching Nayan's territory, he was ordered to leave Mongol, Jurchen, and Han troops to garrison the Hala River.

sentences.zh: 復選精騎扈駕，至失剌斡耳朶，從御史大夫玉速帖木兒討乃顏。

translations.literal: He again selected elite cavalry to escort the imperial carriage to Shilawo'erduo and followed Censor-in-Chief Yusutie'er in punishing Nayan.
translations.idiomatic: He again selected elite cavalry to escort the emperor to Shilawo'erduo and followed Censor-in-Chief Yusutie'er in the campaign against Nayan.

sentences.zh: 七月，至扎剌麻禿，與金家奴戰，敗之，追至蒙可山、那兀江等處，遂平金家奴、塔不台等。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, when they reached Zhalamatu, he fought Jinjianu, defeated him, pursued to Mengke Mountain, Nawujiang, and other places, and thereupon pacified Jinjianu, Tabutai, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, at Zhalamatu, he fought Jinjianu, defeated him, and pursued to Mengke Mountain and Nawujiang, pacifying Jinjianu, Tabutai, and their followers.

sentences.zh: 九月，師還。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the army returned.

sentences.zh: 哈丹、八剌哈赤再叛，十月，重喜從諸王愛牙哈赤、平章塔出、都萬戶闍里鐵木兒征之。

translations.literal: Hadan and Balahachi rebelled again. In the tenth month Chongxi followed Princely Lord Aiyahachi, Chief Councilor Tachu, and Commander-in-Chief Qielitie'er in campaigning against them.
translations.idiomatic: When Hadan and Balahachi rebelled again, in the tenth month Chongxi followed Prince Aiyahachi, Chief Councilor Tachu, and Commander-in-Chief Qielitie'er on the punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 十二月，次木骨不剌。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the army halted at Mugubula.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the army encamped at Mugubula.

sentences.zh: 時諸王脫歡、監司脫台以兵四千餘人與其黨戰，稍却，重喜率騎兵援之，冒鋒陷陣，大破其衆。

translations.literal: At that time Princely Lord Tuohuan and Supervisor Tuotai with more than four thousand troops fought their faction and were slightly driven back. Chongxi led cavalry to their aid, braved the front and broke the enemy ranks, and utterly routed their force.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tuohuan and Supervisor Tuotai, with more than four thousand men, were fighting the rebels and had been pushed back slightly. Chongxi led cavalry to their relief, charged through the enemy line, and broke their force completely.

sentences.zh: 又從諸王乃蠻帶、愛牙哈赤、平章薛闍干，與叛王兵戰于兀朮站，又戰于黑龍江，又戰于貼滿哈處，皆敗之。

translations.literal: He again followed Princely Lords Naimandai and Aiyahachi and Chief Councilor Xuechagan in fighting rebel troops at Wuzhu Station, again on the Amur River, and again at Tiemanha — defeating them each time.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Princes Naimandai and Aiyahachi and Chief Councilor Xuechagan in battles with rebel forces at Wuzhu Station, on the Amur River, and at Tiemanha, defeating them each time.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，重喜又從玉速帖木兒出師，五月，至貼列可，與哈丹禿魯干戰，獲功。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Chongxi again followed Yusutie'er on campaign. In the fifth month, when they reached Tielieke, he fought Hadan Tulugan and won merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year Chongxi again campaigned under Yusutie'er. In the fifth month, at Tielieke, he fought Hadan Tulugan and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 至木骨兒抄剌，又戰。

translations.literal: When they reached Muguerchaola they fought again.
translations.idiomatic: At Muguerchaola they fought again.

sentences.zh: 八月，至貴列河，重喜率兵先涉與戰，勝之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, when they reached Guilie River, Chongxi led troops to cross first and fight, and was victorious.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, at Guilie River, Chongxi led his men across first to give battle and won.

sentences.zh: 十月，又從玉速帖木兒往征木八蘭。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he again followed Yusutie'er to campaign against Mubalan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he again followed Yusutie'er against Mubalan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，與古土禿魯干戰，克之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he fought Gutu Tulugan and overcame him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he fought Gutu Tulugan and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 二十七年六月，賜白金五十兩、甲一襲。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-seventh year he was granted fifty taels of white gold and one suit of armor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-seventh year he was granted fifty taels of white gold and a suit of armor.

sentences.zh: 九月，至禪春，與哈丹禿魯干戰。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, when they reached Chanchun, he fought Hadan Tulugan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, at Chanchun, he fought Hadan Tulugan.

sentences.zh: 二十八年二月，從平章薛闍干至高麗青州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-eighth year he followed Chief Councilor Xuechagan to Qingzhou in Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twenty-eighth year he followed Chief Councilor Xuechagan to Qingzhou in Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 五月，與哈丹戰八日，又戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he fought Hadan for eight days, fought again, and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he fought Hadan for eight days, engaged again, and routed him completely.

sentences.zh: 六月，班師，授昭勇大將軍，佩三珠虎符，職如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the army withdrew. He was appointed General of Manifest Valor, wore a three-pearl tiger tally, and his posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the army withdrew. He was appointed General of Manifest Valor, given a three-pearl tiger tally, and retained his former offices.

sentences.zh: 十月，薛闍干以重喜入朝，且以其功聞，帝嘉之，賜玉帶一、白金五十兩，授龍虎衛上將軍、遼陽等處行中書省右丞。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Xuechagan brought Chongxi to court and reported his achievements. The emperor commended him, granted one jade belt and fifty taels of white gold, and appointed him Tiger-Dragon Guard General and right vice-censor of the Branch Secretariat of Liaoyang and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Xuechagan brought Chongxi to court and reported his achievements. The emperor commended him, granted a jade belt and fifty taels of white gold, and appointed him Tiger-Dragon Guard General and right vice-censor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，仍佩元降虎符，緫管高麗、女直、漢軍萬戶，兼安撫使、高麗軍民緫管。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he still wore the tiger tally for surrendered Yuan troops, commanded ten-thousand-households of Goryeo, Jurchen, and Han troops, and also served as Pacification Commissioner and commissioner-general of Goryeo troops and people.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he still wore the tiger tally for surrendered Yuan troops, commanded the Goryeo, Jurchen, and Han ten-thousand-households, and also served as Pacification Commissioner and commissioner-general over Goryeo troops and people.

sentences.zh: 六月，改資德大夫、遼陽等處行中書省右丞。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was changed to Virtue-Nurturing Grand Master and right vice-censor of the Branch Secretariat of Liaoyang and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was made Virtue-Nurturing Grand Master and right vice-censor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大德十年，以其叔父君祥代之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Dade his uncle Junxiang replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Dade his uncle Junxiang took his place.

sentences.zh: 十一年，武宗即位，重喜朝于上都。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Wuzong acceded; Chongxi had audience at Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when Wuzong took the throne, Chongxi had audience at Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 七月，復授遼陽行省右丞。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was again appointed right vice-censor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was again appointed right vice-censor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，謫漳州，行至杭，遇赦而止。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida he was banished to Zhangzhou; when he reached Hangzhou he met an amnesty and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhida he was banished to Zhangzhou; reaching Hangzhou, he was spared by an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 明年卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 子滋，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Zi inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 鄭鼎，澤州陽城人。

translations.literal: Zheng Ding was a man of Yangcheng in Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Ding was a native of Yangcheng in Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，能自立，讀書曉大義，不妄言笑。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he could stand on his own; he read books and understood great principles, and did not speak or laugh without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he made his own way; he read widely, grasped the larger principles, and never spoke or laughed without reason.

sentences.zh: 既長，勇力過人，尤善騎射。

translations.literal: When grown, his courage and strength surpassed others; he was especially skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, his strength and courage surpassed others, and he was especially skilled in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 初為澤、潞、遼、沁千戶。

translations.literal: At first he was thousand-household of Ze, Lu, Liao, and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as thousand-household over Ze, Lu, Liao, and Qin.

sentences.zh: 歲甲午，從塔海紺不征蜀，攻二里散關，屢立戰功，還屯秦中。

translations.literal: In the jiawu year he followed Tahai Ganbu in campaigning against Shu, attacked Erlisan Pass, repeatedly won battle merit, and returned to garrison Qinzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiawu year he followed Tahai Ganbu in the Shu campaign, attacked Erlisan Pass, won repeated distinction in battle, and returned to garrison the Qin region.

sentences.zh: 未幾，宋將餘侍郎燒絕棧道，以兵圍興元，鼎率衆修復之，破宋兵，解興元之圍。

translations.literal: Before long, Song general Vice Minister Yu burned the plank road and surrounded Xingyuan with troops. Ding led his force to repair it, defeated the Song troops, and lifted the siege of Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, the Song vice minister Yu burned the plank road and besieged Xingyuan. Ding led his men to restore the road, routed the Song force, and lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，遷陽城縣軍民長官。

translations.literal: In yisi he was transferred to be chief official of troops and people in Yangcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: In yisi he was made chief officer over troops and people in Yangcheng County.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，從憲宗征大理國，自六盤山經臨洮，下西蕃諸城，抵雪山，山徑盤屈，舍騎徒步，嘗背負憲宗以行。

translations.literal: In gengxu he followed Emperor Xianzong in campaigning against Dali. From Liupan Mountain they passed through Lintao, descended through the cities of the western Tibetans, and reached Snow Mountain. The mountain paths wound and turned; they left their horses and went on foot, and he once carried Xianzong on his back as they walked.
translations.idiomatic: In gengxu he followed Emperor Xianzong against Dali. From Liupan Mountain they passed Lintao, took the cities of the western Tibetans, and reached Snow Mountain. The paths were tortuous; they dismounted and went on foot, and he once carried the emperor on his back along the trail.

sentences.zh: 敵據扼險要，鼎奮身力戰，敵敗北，帝壯之，賜馬三匹。

translations.literal: The enemy held strategic passes; Ding threw himself into fierce battle, the enemy were defeated and fled north. The emperor admired his valor and granted three horses.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy held the strategic passes. Ding fought with all his strength, routed them, and drove them north. The emperor admired his valor and granted him three horses.

sentences.zh: 至金沙河，波濤洶湧，帝臨水傍危石，立馬觀之。

translations.literal: When they reached the Jinsha River the waves surged violently. The emperor came to the water beside perilous rocks and stood on his horse to watch.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jinsha River the current ran wild. The emperor came to the bank beside treacherous rocks and sat his horse to watch the water.

sentences.zh: 鼎諫曰：「此非聖躬所宜。

translations.literal: Ding remonstrated: "This is not fitting for the sacred person."
translations.idiomatic: Ding remonstrated: "This is no place for Your Majesty's person."

sentences.zh: 」親扶下馬，帝嘉之。

translations.literal: He personally helped him dismount; the emperor commended him.
translations.idiomatic: He helped the emperor down from his horse himself, and the emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 俄圍大理，晝夜急攻，城陷，禽其主，大理平。

translations.literal: Before long they besieged Dali, attacking day and night with urgency. The city fell, its ruler was captured, and Dali was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they besieged Dali, pressing the assault day and night until the city fell, its ruler was taken, and Dali was pacified.

sentences.zh: 師還，命鼎居後。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Ding was ordered to bring up the rear.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march, Ding was ordered to bring up the rear.

sentences.zh: 道經吐蕃，全軍而歸。

translations.literal: Passing through Tibet, he brought the whole army back safely.
translations.idiomatic: Marching through Tibet, he brought the entire force back intact.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，入朝，帝問以時務，鼎敷對詳明，帝嘉納之，賜名曰也可拔都。

translations.literal: In xinhai he came to court. The emperor questioned him on current affairs; Ding answered in detail and with clarity. The emperor commended and accepted his replies and granted him the name Yekebadu.
translations.idiomatic: In xinhai he came to court. The emperor questioned him on affairs of state; Ding answered with detail and clarity. The emperor approved his counsel and granted him the name Yekebadu.

sentences.zh: 己未，賜白金千兩。

translations.literal: In jiwei he was granted one thousand taels of white gold.
translations.idiomatic: In jiwei he was granted one thousand taels of white gold.

sentences.zh: 從世祖南伐，攻大勝關，破之。

translations.literal: He followed Shizu on the southern campaign, attacked Dasheng Pass, and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Kublai on the southern campaign, attacked Dasheng Pass, and took it.

sentences.zh: 繼破臺山寨，禽其守者胡知縣，乘勝獨進，前陷泥淖，遇伏兵突出葭葦間，鼎奮擊，連殺三人，餘衆遁去。

translations.literal: He next broke Taishan Stockade and captured its defender, Magistrate Hu. Pressing the victory he advanced alone, sank into mud ahead, and met ambush troops bursting from among the reeds. Ding fought fiercely, killing three in succession; the rest fled.
translations.idiomatic: He next took Taishan Stockade and captured its defender, Magistrate Hu. Pressing his advantage he advanced alone, sank into mud ahead, and was ambushed from the reeds. Ding fought back fiercely, killing three men in succession; the rest fled.

sentences.zh: 帝急召鼎還，使者以聞，帝曰：「為將當慎重，不可恃勇輕進。

translations.literal: The emperor urgently summoned Ding back. When the messenger reported this, the emperor said: "As a general one must be cautious and cannot rely on courage to advance lightly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor urgently recalled Ding. When the messenger reported what had happened, the emperor said: "A general must be cautious and must not trust in courage alone to press forward recklessly.

sentences.zh: 」遂分畀衛士三百人，以備不虞，且戒之曰：「自今非奉朕命，毋得輕與敵接。

translations.literal: He thereupon allotted him three hundred guards against the unexpected and also admonished him: "From now on, unless you receive my command, you must not lightly engage the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He then assigned him three hundred guards as a precaution and admonished him: "From now on, unless you receive my command, you must not lightly engage the enemy.

sentences.zh: 」秋九月，帝駐蹕江滸，命諸將南渡，先達彼岸者，舉烽火為應，鼎首奪南岸，衆軍畢渡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn the emperor halted at the river bank and ordered the generals to cross south. Whoever reached the far shore first was to raise beacon fires as signal. Ding was first to seize the south bank, and all the armies crossed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn the emperor halted on the riverbank and ordered his generals to cross south. Whoever reached the far shore first was to light beacon fires as signal. Ding was first to seize the south bank, and the whole army crossed.

sentences.zh: 進圍鄂州，戰益力。

translations.literal: Advancing to besiege Ezhou, he fought with increasing force.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to besiege Ezhou, he fought with redoubled vigor.

sentences.zh: 別攻興國軍，遇宋兵五千，力戰破之，擒其將桑太尉，責以懦怯，不忠所事，斬之。

translations.literal: Separately he attacked Xingguo Army, met five thousand Song troops, fought fiercely and broke them, captured their general Grand Marshal Sang, rebuked him for cowardice and disloyalty to his post, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: On a separate front he attacked Xingguo Army, met five thousand Song troops, routed them in fierce fighting, captured their general Grand Marshal Sang, rebuked him for cowardice and disloyalty, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，以功遷平陽、太原兩路萬戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, for his merit he was transferred to be ten-thousand-household of the two circuits of Pingyang and Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong, for his achievements he was made ten-thousand-household of the Pingyang and Taiyuan circuits.

sentences.zh: 阿藍荅兒、渾都海之亂，鼎分率本道兵討之。

translations.literal: In the disorders of Alandai'er and Hunduhai, Ding separately led troops of his circuit to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: During the disorders of Alandai'er and Hunduhai, Ding led troops from his circuit to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔鼎統征西等軍，戍雁門關隘。

translations.literal: In the second year an edict ordered Ding to command the Western Campaign armies and garrison the passes at Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year an edict ordered Ding to command the western campaign armies and garrison the Yanmen passes.

sentences.zh: 遷河東南、北兩路宣撫使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Pacification Commissioner of the southern and northern circuits of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Pacification Commissioner of the southern and northern Hedong circuits.

sentences.zh: 三年，改授平陽太原宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was changed to Pacification and Comfort Commissioner of Pingyang and Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Pacification and Comfort Commissioner of Pingyang and Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 至元三年，遷平陽路緫管。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiyuan he was transferred to commissioner of Pingyang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhiyuan he was made commissioner of Pingyang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 是歲大旱，鼎下車而雨。

translations.literal: That year there was great drought; when Ding stepped down from his carriage, rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: That year a great drought struck; when Ding stepped down from his carriage, rain fell.

sentences.zh: 平陽地狹人衆，常乏食，鼎乃導汾水，溉民田千餘頃，開潞河鵬黃嶺道，以來上黨之粟。

translations.literal: Pingyang's land was narrow and its people numerous; food was often scarce. Ding therefore channeled the Fen River to irrigate more than a thousand qing of fields and opened the Peng Huangling road on the Lu River to bring grain from Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyang was crowded on little land and often short of food. Ding channeled the Fen River to irrigate more than a thousand qing of fields and opened the Peng Huangling road on the Lu River to bring grain from Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 修學校，厲風俗，建橫澗故橋以便行旅，民德之。

translations.literal: He repaired schools, strengthened customs, and built the old bridge at Hengjian to ease travelers; the people were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: He restored schools, improved local customs, and rebuilt the old bridge at Hengjian for travelers; the people were grateful.

sentences.zh: 七年，改僉書西蜀四川行尚書省事，將兵巡東川。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was changed to secretary of the Western Shu Sichuan Branch Secretariat and led troops on patrol in eastern Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made secretary of the Western Shu Sichuan Branch Secretariat and led troops on patrol in eastern Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 過嘉定，遇蜀兵，與戰江中，擒其將李越，悉獲戰船。

translations.literal: Passing Jiading he met Shu troops, fought them on the river, captured their general Li Yue, and took all their warships.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Jiading he met Shu forces, fought them on the river, captured their general Li Yue, and seized all their warships.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，改軍前行尚書省事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year he was changed to secretary of the Forward Army Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year he was made secretary of the Forward Army Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十一年，從伐宋。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he followed the campaign against Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he joined the campaign against Song.

sentences.zh: 十二年，鎮黃州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he garrisoned Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was posted to garrison Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，改授淮西宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer he was changed to Pacification and Comfort Commissioner of Huai West.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he was made Pacification and Comfort Commissioner of Huai West.

sentences.zh: 十三年，加昭毅大將軍，賜白金五百兩。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was advanced to Majestic Resolution General and granted five hundred taels of white gold.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was advanced to Majestic Resolution General and granted five hundred taels of white gold.

sentences.zh: 十四年，改湖北道宣慰使，移鎮鄂州。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was changed to Pacification and Comfort Commissioner of the Hubei Circuit and transferred his garrison to Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was made Pacification and Comfort Commissioner of the Hubei Circuit and moved his base to Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，蘄、黃二州叛，鼎將兵討之，戰于樊口，舟覆溺死，年六十有三。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer Qi and Huang prefectures rebelled. Ding led troops to punish them, fought at Fankou, his boat capsized, and he drowned at age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer Qi and Huang rebelled. Ding led troops against them, fought at Fankou, capsized and drowned at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 十七年，董文忠等奏：「鄭也可拔都遇害，其叛人家屬物產，宜悉與其子納懷。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Dong Wenzhong and others memorialized: "Zheng Yekebadu met with violence; the families and property of the rebels should all be given to his son Nahuan."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Dong Wenzhong and others memorialized: "Zheng Yekebadu was killed in the line of duty; the families and property of the rebels should all be given to his son Nahuan."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 贈中書右丞，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted right vice-censor of the Secretariat with the posthumous title Loyal and Resolute.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made right vice-censor of the Secretariat with the posthumous epithet Loyal and Resolute.

sentences.zh: 後加贈宣忠保節功臣、平章政事、柱國，追封潞國公，諡忠肅。

translations.literal: Later he was further posthumously granted the title Merit-Preserving Loyal and Faithful Minister, chief councilor, and Pillar of the State, enfeoffed as Duke of Lu State with the posthumous title Loyal and Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was further granted the title Merit-Preserving Loyal and Faithful Minister, chief councilor, and Pillar of the State, enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Lu with the epithet Loyal and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 子制宜。

translations.literal: His son was Zhiyi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhiyi.

sentences.zh: 制宜小字納懷，性聰敏，莊重有器局，通習國語。

translations.literal: Zhiyi's childhood name was Nahuan. He was clever by nature, grave and possessed of breadth of vision, and fluent in the national language.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi, whose childhood name was Nahuan, was clever by nature, grave and far-seeing, and fluent in Mongolian.

sentences.zh: 至元十四年，襲父職太原、平陽萬戶，仍戍鄂州。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan he inherited his father's post as ten-thousand-household of Taiyuan and Pingyang and still garrisoned Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan he inherited his father's post as ten-thousand-household of Taiyuan and Pingyang and continued to garrison Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 時鄂闕守，俾攝府事。

translations.literal: At that time Ezhou lacked a defender; he was made to administer prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ezhou then lacked a permanent defender, so he was put in charge of prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 十九年，朝廷將征日本，造樓船何家洲。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the court was about to campaign against Japan and built tower ships at Hejiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, as the court prepared to campaign against Japan, tower ships were built at Hejiazhou.

sentences.zh: 洲地狹，衆欲徙旁居民，制宜不從，改授寬地，居民德之。

translations.literal: The islet was narrow; the crowd wished to move nearby residents, but Zhiyi would not agree and instead assigned wider ground; the residents were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: The islet was cramped and many wished to relocate nearby residents, but Zhiyi refused and assigned a wider site instead; the people were grateful.

sentences.zh: 城中屢災，或言于制宜曰：「恐姦人乘間為變，宜捕其疑似者，痛治之。

translations.literal: Disasters struck the city repeatedly. Someone said to Zhiyi: "I fear wrongdoers may seize the opportunity to make trouble; you should arrest those who seem suspicious and punish them severely."
translations.idiomatic: Disasters struck the city repeatedly. Someone urged Zhiyi: "Wrongdoers may seize the chance to stir trouble — you should arrest those who seem suspicious and punish them severely."

sentences.zh: 」制宜曰：「吾但嚴守備而已，奈何濫及無辜！

translations.literal: Zhiyi said: "I need only tighten defenses — why drag in the innocent!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi said: "I need only tighten our defenses — why sweep up the innocent!"

sentences.zh: 」不笞一人，災亦遂息。

translations.literal: He did not flog a single person, and the disasters also soon ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He did not punish a single person, and the disasters soon ceased as well.

sentences.zh: 有盜伏近郊，晨暮剽劫，流言將入城。

translations.literal: Bandits lurked in the nearby suburbs, robbing at dawn and dusk; rumor spread that they would enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits lurked in the nearby suburbs, raiding at dawn and dusk, and rumor spread that they would enter the city.

sentences.zh: 俄有數男子自城外至，顧盻異常，制宜命吏縛入獄，問之無驗，行省疑其非，將釋之，不從。

translations.literal: Before long several men arrived from outside the city; their glances were unusual. Zhiyi ordered clerks to bind them and put them in prison. Questioning yielded no proof. The Branch Secretariat doubted they were guilty and was about to release them; he would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Soon several men arrived from outside the city with suspicious looks. Zhiyi had them bound and jailed. Interrogation turned up no evidence, and the Branch Secretariat, suspecting they were innocent, moved to release them — but he refused.

sentences.zh: 明日，再出城東，遇一人，乘白馬，貌服殊異，制宜叱下，訊之，乃與前數男子同為盜者，遂正其罪，一郡帖然。

translations.literal: The next day, going out east of the city again, he encountered a man riding a white horse whose appearance and dress were very unusual. Zhiyi shouted him down, interrogated him, and learned he was a bandit together with the several men before; he then carried out proper punishment on them, and the whole commandery became settled.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, going out east of the city again, he met a man on a white horse whose dress and bearing were strikingly odd. Zhiyi pulled him down and questioned him — he turned out to be in league with the men from before. Zhiyi punished them by law, and the whole commandery settled down.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，扈駕東征乃顏，請赴敵自效。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he accompanied the emperor on the eastern campaign against Nayan and requested to go against the enemy and serve with his life.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he accompanied the emperor on the eastern campaign against Nayan and volunteered to fight the enemy in person.

sentences.zh: 帝顧左右曰：「而父歿王事，惟有一子，毋使在行陣。

translations.literal: The emperor looked to those beside him and said: "Your father died in the king's service; you are his only son — do not let him be in the battle line."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to those beside him and said: "Your father died in the service of the throne, and you are his only son — keep him out of the fighting."

sentences.zh: 」制宜請愈力，乃命從月兒呂那顏別為一軍，以戰功授懷遠大將軍、樞密院判官。

translations.literal: Zhiyi pressed his request all the more earnestly; he was then ordered to follow Yue'erbü Nayen as a separate army, and for battle merit was granted General for Expanding the Realm and associate censor of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi pressed his request all the harder, and was at last ordered to serve under Yue'erbü Nayen in a separate command. For his battle merit he was made General for Expanding the Realm and associate censor of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年，車駕幸上都。

translations.literal: The next year the imperial carriage visited Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor traveled to Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 舊制：樞府官從行，歲留一員司本院事，漢人不得與。

translations.literal: Under the old rule: Bureau of Military Affairs officials accompanied the emperor on campaign; each year one officer remained to manage the bureau's affairs — Han Chinese were not permitted to serve in this capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rule, when Bureau of Military Affairs officials accompanied the emperor, one officer stayed behind each year to manage bureau affairs — and Han Chinese were excluded.

sentences.zh: 至是，以屬制宜。

translations.literal: At this time the duty was assigned to Zhiyi.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion the post was given to Zhiyi.

sentences.zh: 制宜遜辭，帝曰：「汝豈漢人比耶！

translations.literal: Zhiyi declined with modesty. The emperor said: "How can you be compared to Han Chinese!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi politely declined. The emperor said: "You are no ordinary Han Chinese!"

sentences.zh: 」竟留之。

translations.literal: In the end he was kept there.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was kept at his post.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，遷湖廣行省參知政事，陛辭，帝曰：「汝父死王事，賞未汝及。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was transferred to be vice administrator of the Huguang Branch Secretariat. At his audience of leave the emperor said: "Your father died in the king's service, and the reward has not yet reached you."
