translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was made vice administrator of the Huguang Branch Secretariat. When he took leave at court, the emperor said: "Your father died in the service of the throne, and you have not yet received the reward due you."

sentences.zh: 近者，要束木伏誅，已籍沒其財產人畜，汝可擇其佳者取之。

translations.literal: Recently Yao Somu was executed; his property, livestock, and goods have been confiscated and registered — you may pick out the fine ones and take them.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Yao Somu was executed and his property and livestock confiscated — you may choose the best of them for yourself.

sentences.zh: 」制宜對曰：「彼以贓敗，臣復取之，寧無污乎！

translations.literal: Zhiyi replied: "Since he was ruined through corruption, if I take from him again, would I not be stained!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi replied: "He fell through corruption — if I take from his estate, would that not stain me as well?"

sentences.zh: 」帝賢其所守，賜白金五千兩。

translations.literal: The emperor admired his integrity and granted him five thousand taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his integrity and rewarded him with five thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 未幾，徵拜內臺侍御史。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned and appointed attendant censor of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was summoned and appointed attendant censor of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 安西舊有牧地，圉人恃勢，冒奪民田十萬餘頃，訟于有司，積年不能理。

translations.literal: Anxi formerly had pasture lands; stockmen relied on power and falsely seized more than a hundred thousand qing of civilian fields. They litigated before the appropriate offices for years without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: Anxi had long had pasture lands, and stockmen used their influence to encroach on more than a hundred thousand qing of civilian farmland. Cases dragged on for years in the local courts with no resolution.

sentences.zh: 制宜奉詔而往，按圖籍以正之，訟由是息。

translations.literal: Zhiyi received the edict and went; he corrected matters according to register maps and records, and litigation thereby ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi went as ordered, set matters right according to official maps and registers, and the lawsuits ended.

sentences.zh: 大德八年，晉地大震，平陽尤甚，壓死者衆，制宜承命存恤，懼緩不及事，晝夜倍道兼行，至則親入里巷，撫瘡殘，給粟帛，存者賴之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dade, Jin territory shook greatly in an earthquake; Pingyang was especially severe, and many were crushed to death. Zhiyi received orders to bring relief and aid; fearing delay would miss the need, he traveled day and night at double speed. Upon arrival he personally entered lanes and alleys, comforted the wounded and ruined, gave grain and cloth, and those who survived relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dade a great earthquake struck Jin territory, worst in Pingyang, killing many. Ordered to bring relief, Zhiyi feared any delay and pushed on day and night. When he arrived he went personally into the lanes, comforted the wounded, distributed grain and cloth, and the survivors owed him their lives.

sentences.zh: 成宗素知其名，眷遇殊厚，每侍宴，輒不敢飲，終日無惰容，帝察其忠勤，屢賜內醞，輒持以奉母，帝聞之，特封其母蘇氏為潞國太夫人。

translations.literal: Emperor Chengzong had long known his name and treated him with exceptional favor. Whenever he attended banquets he dared not drink; all day he showed no slack demeanor. The emperor observed his loyalty and diligence and repeatedly granted him imperial wine; he always carried it off to serve his mother. When the emperor heard of this, he specially enfeoffed his mother Lady Su as Grand Lady of Lu State.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chengzong had long known his reputation and treated him with special favor. At banquets he would not touch wine and never showed a slack face all day. Noting his loyalty and diligence, the emperor repeatedly sent him imperial wine, which he always brought home to his mother. Hearing this, the emperor ennobled his mother Lady Su as Grand Lady of Lu.

sentences.zh: 十年，制宜以疾終，年四十有七。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Zhiyi died of illness at age forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Zhiyi died of illness at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈推忠贊治功臣、銀青榮祿大夫、平章政事，追封澤國公，諡忠宣。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Merit-Honoring Loyal and Governance-Supporting Minister, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver and Blue, chief councilor, enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Ze State with the posthumous title Loyal and Proclaiming.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made a Merit-Honoring Loyal and Governance-Supporting minister, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver and Blue, and chief councilor, enfeoffed as Duke of Ze with the epithet Loyal and Proclaiming.

sentences.zh: 子阿兒思蘭嗣。

translations.literal: His son Arsalan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Arsalan succeeded to his post.

sentences.zh: 李進，保定曲陽人。

translations.literal: Li Jin was a man of Quyang in Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jin was from Quyang in Baoding.

sentences.zh: 幼隸軍籍，初從萬戶張柔屯杞之三叉口，時荊山之西九十里曰龍岡者，宋境也。

translations.literal: In youth he was enrolled in the military register. At first he followed the ten-thousand-household Zhang Rou, garrisoned at Sankoukou in Qi. At that time ninety li west of Jingshan was a place called Longgang — Song territory.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the military register as a youth. He first served under the ten-thousand-household Zhang Rou, encamped at Sankoukou in Qi. Ninety li west of Jingshan lay Longgang — Song territory.

sentences.zh: 歲庚戌春，張柔引兵築堡岡上。

translations.literal: In the gengxu year, spring, Zhang Rou led troops to build a fort on the hill.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengxu year, in spring, Zhang Rou led troops to build a fort atop the hill.

sentences.zh: 會淮水汎漲，宋以舟師卒至，主帥察罕率軍逆戰，進以兵十五人載一舟，轉鬪十餘里，奪一巨艦，遂以功陞百戶。

translations.literal: When the Huai River flooded and rose, Song sent a fleet that suddenly arrived. Commander-in-chief Chaghan led the army to meet them in battle. Jin put fifteen soldiers in one boat, fought in circles for more than ten li, seized one great warship, and thereby for merit was promoted to hundred-household.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huai flooded, Song warships arrived suddenly. Commander Chaghan met them in battle. Jin loaded fifteen men to a boat, fought for more than ten li, and seized a great warship. For this he was promoted to hundred-household.

sentences.zh: 戊午，憲宗西征，丞相史天澤時為河南經略大使，選諸道兵之驍勇者從，遂命進為緫把。

translations.literal: In wuwu, Emperor Xianzong campaigned west. Chief councilor Shi Tianze was then Pacification Commissioner of Henan; he selected the brave and fierce from troops of all circuits to follow, and thus ordered Jin to be chief corporal.
translations.idiomatic: In wuwu, during Emperor Xianzong's western campaign, Chief Councilor Shi Tianze, then Pacification Commissioner of Henan, picked the fiercest troops from every circuit — and appointed Jin chief corporal.

sentences.zh: 是年秋九月，道由陳倉入興元，度米倉關，其地荒塞不通，進伐木開道七百餘里。

translations.literal: That year in autumn, the ninth month, the route went from Chencang into Xingyuan and crossed Micang Pass. The region was desolate and blocked; Jin felled trees and opened a road of more than seven hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, in the ninth month, the army went from Chencang into Xingyuan and crossed Micang Pass through wilderness where no road existed. Jin cleared trees and opened a path more than seven hundred li long.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，至定遠七十關，其關上下皆築連堡，宋以五百人守之，巴渠江水環堡東流。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, they reached Dingyuan's Seventy Pass. Above and below the pass chained forts were all built; Song defended with five hundred men. Baju River water circled the fort flowing east.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter they reached Dingyuan's Seventy Pass, where chained forts lined the heights above and below. Song garrisoned it with five hundred men, and the Baju River curled eastward around the forts.

sentences.zh: 天澤命進往關下說降之，不從。

translations.literal: Tianze ordered Jin to go below the pass and persuade them to surrender; they would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Tianze sent Jin to the pass to offer terms; they refused.

sentences.zh: 進潛視間道，歸白天澤曰：「彼可取也。

translations.literal: Jin secretly surveyed a hidden path, returned, and reported to Tianze: "They can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Jin reconnoitered a hidden route and reported to Tianze: "They can be taken."

sentences.zh: 」是夜二鼓，天澤遣進率勇士七十人，掩其不備，攻之，脫門樞而入者二十人。

translations.literal: That night at the second watch Tianze dispatched Jin leading seventy brave men to strike them unprepared and attack. Twenty men removed the door pivot and entered.
translations.idiomatic: That night at the second watch Tianze sent Jin with seventy picked men for a surprise attack. Twenty men pried out the door pivot and got inside.

sentences.zh: 守門者覺，拔刀拒之，進被傷，不以為病。

translations.literal: The gate guards noticed, drew swords to resist; Jin was wounded but did not regard it as ailment.
translations.idiomatic: The guards noticed and drew swords to hold them off. Jin was wounded but paid it no mind.

sentences.zh: 懸門俄閉，諸軍不得入，進與二十人力戰，殺傷三十人。

translations.literal: The hanging gate soon closed; the various armies could not enter. Jin and the twenty men fought with all their strength, killing and wounding thirty men.
translations.idiomatic: The portcullis slammed shut and the main force could not enter. Jin and his twenty men fought on, killing and wounding thirty.

sentences.zh: 後兵走上堡，進乃毀懸門，納諸軍，追至上堡，殺傷益衆，宋兵不能敵，棄走。

translations.literal: The rear troops went up to the upper fort; Jin then destroyed the hanging gate, admitted the various armies, pursued to the upper fort — killed and wounded were even more numerous. Song troops could not resist and fled abandoning the position.
translations.idiomatic: The main body fought its way to the upper fort. Jin broke down the portcullis and let the rest in, then pursued to the upper fort, killing and wounding many more. The Song force could not hold and fled.

sentences.zh: 夜將旦，進遂得其堡，守之，關路始通，諸軍盡度。

translations.literal: When night was nearly dawn Jin secured their fort and held it; the pass route was first opened and all armies fully crossed.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn Jin had taken the fort and held it. The pass was finally open and the whole army crossed.

sentences.zh: 進以功受上賞。

translations.literal: Jin for merit received highest reward.
translations.idiomatic: Jin received the highest reward for his service.

sentences.zh: 己未春二月，天澤兵至行在所，圍合州釣魚山寨。

translations.literal: In jiwei, spring, the second month, Tianze's army reached the mobile court and besieged Hezhou's Diaoyu Mountain Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: In jiwei, in the second month of spring, Tianze's army reached the emperor's camp and besieged Diaoyu Mountain Fortress at Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，宋由嘉陵江以舟師來援，始大戰三槽山西。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, Song came to aid by the Jialing River with a fleet; the first great battle was west of Sancao Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer Song relief came up the Jialing by river. The first great battle was fought west of Sancao Mountain.

sentences.zh: 六月，戰山之東，有功。

translations.literal: In the sixth month they fought east of the mountain and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month they fought east of the mountain with success.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，宋兵戰艦三百餘泊黑石峽東，以輕舟五十為前鋒，北軍之船七十餘泊峽西，相距一里許。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, more than three hundred Song battle warships anchored east of Heishi Gorge; fifty light boats served as vanguard. More than seventy northern army boats anchored west of the gorge, about one li apart.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn more than three hundred Song warships lay east of Heishi Gorge, fifty light craft in the vanguard. More than seventy northern boats lay west of the gorge, barely a li apart.

sentences.zh: 帝立馬東山，擁兵二萬，夾江而陣，天澤乃號令於衆曰：「聽吾鼓，視吾旗，無少怠也。

translations.literal: The emperor stood horse on East Mountain with twenty thousand troops arrayed along both banks of the river. Tianze then issued commands to the crowd: "Listen to my drums, watch my flags — let there be no slightest slack."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took position on East Mountain with twenty thousand men lined up on both banks. Tianze cried to the host: "Watch my drums and flags — not a moment's slack!"

sentences.zh: 」頃之，聞鼓聲，視其旗東指，諸軍遂鼓譟而入，兵一交，宋前鋒潰走，戰艦繼亂，順流縱擊，死者不可勝計。

translations.literal: Before long drums sounded; seeing the flags point east, the various armies then drummed and clamored as they entered. Once forces clashed, Song's vanguard broke and fled; battle warships followed in disorder. They drove downstream in pursuit; the dead were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the drums sounded and the flags swung east. The army roared forward, and at first contact Song's vanguard broke and fled. The warships behind fell into chaos as the northerners drove downstream — the dead were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 帝指顧謂諸將曰：「白旗下服紅半臂突而前者，誰也？

translations.literal: The emperor pointed and looked, saying to the generals: "Under the white banner, the one in the red half-sleeve surging forward — who is he?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pointed and asked the generals: "Who is that man under the white banner in the red half-sleeve charging ahead?"

sentences.zh: 」天澤以進對，賞錦衣、名馬。

translations.literal: Tianze answered with Jin; he was rewarded with brocade robes and a famous horse.
translations.idiomatic: Tianze named Jin, who was rewarded with brocade robes and a fine horse.

sentences.zh: 八月，又戰浮圖關，前後凡五戰，皆以功受上賞。

translations.literal: In the eighth month they fought again at Fotu Pass; in all five battles before and after, he each time for merit received highest reward.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month they fought again at Fotu Pass. Over five engagements in all he earned the highest reward each time.

sentences.zh: 子雯，襲授武德將軍、左翼屯田萬戶，佩虎符。

translations.literal: His son Wen inherited appointment as Martial Virtue General and Left-Wing Agricultural Garrison Ten-Thousand-Household, wearing the tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wen inherited the posts of Martial Virtue General and Left-Wing Agricultural Garrison Ten-Thousand-Household, bearing the tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 皇慶二年，加宣武將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangqing he was promoted to Martial Proclamation General.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangqing he was promoted to Martial Proclamation General.

sentences.zh: 延祐六年，仁宗念其父進嘗北征被掠，特賜雯中統鈔五百錠以恤之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yanyou Emperor Renzong recalled that his father Jin had once on the northern campaign been captured and plundered; he specially granted Wen five hundred ding of Zhongtong notes to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yanyou, recalling that Wen's father Jin had been captured on a northern campaign, Emperor Renzong specially granted Wen five hundred ding of Zhongtong notes as relief.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年春，以疾辭。

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of Taiding he resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Taiding he resigned due to illness.

sentences.zh: 子朶耳只襲。

translations.literal: His son Duo'erzhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duo'erzhi succeeded to the post.

sentences.zh: 石抹按只

translations.literal: Shi Mo Anzhi
translations.idiomatic: Shi Mo Anzhi

sentences.zh: 石抹按只，契丹人，世居太原。

translations.literal: Shi Mo Anzhi was a Khitan whose family had long resided in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Mo Anzhi was a Khitan whose family had lived in Taiyuan for generations.

sentences.zh: 父大家奴，率漢軍五百人歸太祖。

translations.literal: His father Dajianu led five hundred Han army troops to submit to Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dajianu brought five hundred Han troops over to Taizu.

sentences.zh: 歲戊午，按只代領其軍，從都元帥紐璘攻成都。

translations.literal: In the wuwu year Anzhi replaced him in leading their army, following the commander-in-chief Nüchén in attacking Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In wuwu, Anzhi took command of the unit and followed Commander-in-Chief Nüchén against Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 時宋兵聚於靈泉，按只以所部兵與戰，大敗之，殺其將韓都統。

translations.literal: At that time Song troops gathered at Lingquan; Anzhi with his unit's troops fought them, greatly defeated them, and killed their general Han Dutong.
translations.idiomatic: Song forces had massed at Lingquan. Anzhi met them with his command, routed them, and killed their general Han Dutong.

sentences.zh: 又從都元帥按敦攻瀘州，按只以戰艦七十艘至馬湖江，宋軍先以五百艘控扼江渡，按只擊敗之。

translations.literal: Again he followed the commander-in-chief Andun in attacking Luzhou. Anzhi with seventy battle warships reached Ma Lake River; Song troops first with five hundred vessels controlled and blocked the river crossing — Anzhi defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Commander-in-Chief Andun against Luzhou. Anzhi brought seventy warships to the Ma Lake River, where Song had five hundred vessels blocking the crossing — and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 時宋兵於沿江撤橋據守，按只相地形，造浮橋，師至無留行。

translations.literal: At that time Song troops along the river pulled up bridges and held positions; Anzhi assessed the terrain, built pontoon bridges, and when the army arrived there was no delay in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Song forces had dismantled bridges along the river and held the line. Anzhi read the terrain, built pontoon bridges, and the army moved without delay.

sentences.zh: 宋欲撓其役，兵出輒敗，自馬湖以達合江、涪江、清江，凡立浮橋二十餘所。

translations.literal: Song wished to disrupt the work; whenever troops came out they were defeated. From Ma Lake reaching Hejiang, Fujiang, and Qingjiang — in all more than twenty pontoon bridges were erected.
translations.idiomatic: Song tried to disrupt the work but lost every sortie. From the Ma Lake line through Hejiang, Fujiang, and Qingjiang, he put up more than twenty pontoon bridges.

sentences.zh: 及四川平，浮橋之功居多。

translations.literal: When Sichuan was pacified, the merit of the pontoon bridges was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: When Sichuan was pacified, the pontoon bridges accounted for much of the credit.

sentences.zh: 己未，宋以巨艦載甲士數萬，屯清江浮橋，相距七十日。

translations.literal: In jiwei, Song with great warships loaded tens of thousands of armored soldiers, encamped at the Qingjiang pontoon bridge — the two sides faced each other for seventy days.
translations.idiomatic: In jiwei Song brought tens of thousands of armored men on great warships to the Qingjiang pontoon bridge. The two sides faced off for seventy days.

sentences.zh: 水暴漲，浮橋壞，西岸軍多漂溺，按只軍東岸，急撤浮橋，聚舟岸下，士卒得不死，又援出別部軍五百餘人。

translations.literal: The water suddenly rose violently; the pontoon bridge was destroyed. Many on the western bank army were swept and drowned. Anzhi's army was on the eastern bank; he urgently withdrew the pontoon bridge and gathered boats below the shore — soldiers thereby did not die. He also rescued out more than five hundred troops of separate units.
translations.idiomatic: When floodwaters surged and wrecked the bridge, many western-bank troops were swept away. Anzhi was on the east bank; he quickly pulled up the bridge, mustered boats below the shore, and saved his men — and pulled more than five hundred stranded troops to safety.

sentences.zh: 先鋒奔察火魯赤以聞，憲宗遣使慰諭，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Vanguard Benchahuo'lüchi reported it; Emperor Xianzong dispatched envoys to comfort and instruct; rewards were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard commander Benchahuo'lüchi reported the affair. Emperor Xianzong sent envoys with condolences and lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 敘州守將橫截江津，軍不得渡，按只聚軍中牛皮，作渾脫及皮船，乘之與戰，破其軍，奪其渡口，為浮橋以濟師。

translations.literal: The Xuzhou defending general blocked the river crossing horizontally; the army could not cross. Anzhi gathered cowhides from the army, made inflated hides and leather boats, rode them to fight, broke their army, seized their crossing, and built a pontoon bridge to ferry the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuzhou defender blocked the river crossing and the army could not get across. Anzhi gathered army cowhides, made inflated hides and skin boats, fought his way through, seized the ford, and built a pontoon bridge to ferry the troops over.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，授河中府船橋水手軍緫管，佩金符，以立浮橋功也。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong he was appointed chief commander of the Hezhong Prefecture Boat-Bridge Sailor Army, wearing the gold tally — for the merit of building pontoon bridges.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhongtong he was made chief commander of the Hezhong Prefecture boat-bridge sailor corps and given a gold tally for his pontoon-bridge service.

sentences.zh: 至元四年，從行省也速帶兒攻瀘州，按只以水軍與宋將陳都統、張緫制戰于馬湖江，按只身被二創，戰愈力，敗之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan he followed the Branch Secretariat chief Yisudaier in attacking Luzhou. Anzhi with the water army fought Song generals Chen Dutong and Zhang Zongzhi at Ma Lake River. Anzhi's body received two wounds but fought all the harder and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan he followed the branch secretariat chief Yisudaier against Luzhou. At the Ma Lake River he fought Song generals Chen Dutong and Zhang Zongzhi with the naval force. Wounded twice, he fought harder still and routed them.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，也速帶兒領兵趨瀘州，遣按只以舟運其器械、糧食，由水道進。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, first month, Yisudaier led troops pressing toward Luzhou and dispatched Anzhi to transport by boats their equipment and grain, advancing by water route.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year Yisudaier marched on Luzhou and sent Anzhi to bring up weapons and grain by boat along the waterways.

sentences.zh: 宋兵復扼馬湖江，按只擊敗之，生獲四十人，奪其船五艘，復以水軍一千，運糧於眉、簡二州，軍中賴之。

translations.literal: Song troops again blocked Ma Lake River; Anzhi defeated them, captured forty alive, seized five of their boats, and again with one thousand water troops transported grain to Mei and Jian prefectures — the army relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: When Song blocked the Ma Lake River again, Anzhi beat them back, took forty prisoners, captured five boats, and with a thousand sailors brought grain to Mei and Jian — the army depended on him.

sentences.zh: 九年，從征建都蠻，歲餘不下，按只先登其城，力戰，遂降之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he followed the campaign against Jiandu Man. For more than a year they could not take it down. Anzhi was first to mount the city, fought with full strength, and thereby made them surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he joined the campaign against the Jiandu tribes. After more than a year without success, Anzhi was first over the wall, fought fiercely, and the place surrendered.

sentences.zh: 軍還，道病卒。

translations.literal: The army returned; on the road he sickened and died.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he fell ill on the road and died.

sentences.zh: 行省承制以其子不老代領其軍。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat, by provisional order, had his son Bulao replace him in leading their army.
translations.idiomatic: The branch secretariat provisionally appointed his son Bulao to command the unit.

sentences.zh: 不老從攻嘉定，以巨艦七十艘載勇士數千人，據其上流，於府江紅崖灘造浮橋以渡。

translations.literal: Bulao followed in attacking Jiading with seventy great warships carrying several thousand brave men, holding the upper stream; at Hongya Beach on Fujiang he built a pontoon bridge to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Bulao joined the assault on Jiading with seventy great ships carrying several thousand warriors, holding the upstream. At Hongya Beach on the Fujiang he built a pontoon bridge to cross.

sentences.zh: 十二年，嘉定降，宋將鮮于都統率衆遁，不老追至大佛灘，盡斃之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Jiading surrendered. Song general Xianyu Dutong led the crowd in flight; Bulao pursued to Dafo Beach and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Jiading surrendered. Song General Xianyu fled with his men; Bulao chased them to Dafo Beach and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 行院汪田哥攻取紫雲、瀘、敘等城，不老功最多。

translations.literal: Branch yuan Wang Tiange took Ziyun, Lu, Xu, and other cities; Bulao's merit was the greatest.
translations.idiomatic: When branch commander Wang Tiange took Ziyun, Lu, Xu, and other cities, Bulao's contribution was the greatest.

sentences.zh: 及諸軍圍重慶，不老先以戰艦三百艘列陣於觀灘，絕其走路。

translations.literal: When the various armies besieged Chongqing, Bulao first with three hundred battle warships arrayed at Guantan Beach, cutting off their escape routes.
translations.idiomatic: When the army besieged Chongqing, Bulao first lined up three hundred warships at Guantan Beach and cut off the enemy's escape.

sentences.zh: 十三年，領隨翼軍五百人，會招討藥剌海，豎柵於白水江岸以為備。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he led five hundred troops of the attendant wing, joined the pacification commissioner Yao Lihai, and erected palisades on the Baishui River bank as defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he led five hundred wing troops, joined Pacification Commissioner Yao Lihai, and threw up palisades on the Baishui River bank.

sentences.zh: 不老乘夜襲宋軍，直抵重慶城下，攻千斯門，宋軍驚潰，溺死者衆，生擒三十餘人，獲其旗幟甲仗以獻。

translations.literal: Bulao by night raided Song troops, went straight to below Chongqing city wall, attacked Qiansi Gate. Song troops were startled and broke; many drowned. More than thirty were captured alive; he obtained their banners, flags, and armor and weapons and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Bulao raided the Song camp by night, drove straight to the walls of Chongqing, and struck Qiansi Gate. The Song force broke in panic; many drowned. He took more than thirty prisoners and presented their banners, armor, and weapons.

sentences.zh: 宋涪州守將率舟師來援，不老擊敗之於廣陽埧，生獲六十餘人，奪其船十艘。

translations.literal: The Song Fuzhou defending general led a fleet to aid; Bulao defeated them at Guangyang Ba, captured more than sixty alive, and seized ten of their boats.
translations.idiomatic: The Fuzhou defender brought a fleet to relieve the city; Bulao beat him at Guangyang Ba, took more than sixty prisoners, and captured ten boats.

sentences.zh: 十四年，從攻瀘州，不老勒所部兵攻神臂門，蟻附以登，斬首五十級。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he followed the attack on Luzhou. Bulao drove his unit to attack Shenbi Gate, climbing like ants to mount, and beheaded fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he joined the Luzhou campaign. Bulao led his men against Shenbi Gate, swarming up the walls like ants, and took fifty heads.

sentences.zh: 明日復戰，破之。

translations.literal: The next day they fought again and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they fought again and routed them.

sentences.zh: 十五年，復攻重慶太平門，不老先登，殺其守陴卒數十人，宋都統趙安以城降，緫管黃亮乘舟遁，不老追擒之，及其兵士五十人，奪戰艦五十艘。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year they again attacked Chongqing's Taiping Gate. Bulao was first to mount, killed several tens of wall-defending soldiers. Song dutong Zhao An surrendered the city; chief commander Huang Liang escaped by boat. Bulao pursued, captured him and fifty of his soldiers, and seized fifty battle warships.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year they attacked Chongqing's Taiping Gate again. Bulao was first over the wall and killed dozens of defenders. Song Colonel Zhao An surrendered the city; Commander Huang Liang fled by boat. Bulao caught him along with fifty of his men and seized fifty warships.

sentences.zh: 十六年，命襲父職，為懷遠大將軍、船橋軍馬緫管，更賜金虎符，兼夔路鎮守副萬戶。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was ordered to inherit his father's post as General for Expanding the Realm and chief commander of the Boat-Bridge Army and Horses; he was again granted a gold tiger tally and concurrently made deputy ten-thousand-household for garrisoning Kuizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he inherited his father's posts as General for Expanding the Realm and chief commander of the boat-bridge corps, received a new gold tiger tally, and was made deputy ten-thousand-household for the Kuizhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 十八年，大小盤諸峒蠻叛，命領諸翼蒙古、漢軍三千餘人戍施州，既而蠻酋向貴、誓用等降，其餘峒蠻之未服者悉平，遂以為保寧等處萬戶。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the various cave tribes of Dapan and Xiaopan rebelled. He was ordered to lead more than three thousand Mongol and Han troops of the various wings to garrison Shizhou. Before long the barbarian chiefs Xiang Gui, Shiyong, and others surrendered; the remaining cave tribes that had not submitted were all pacified. He was then made ten-thousand-household of Baoning and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the Dapan and Xiaopan cave tribes rebelled. He was sent with more than three thousand Mongol and Han wing troops to garrison Shizhou. Chiefs Xiang Gui and Shiyong soon surrendered, the holdouts were all pacified, and he was made ten-thousand-household of Baoning.

sentences.zh: 謁只里

translations.literal: Ye Zhili
translations.idiomatic: Ye Zhili

sentences.zh: 謁只里，女直人也。

translations.literal: Ye Zhili was a Jurchen.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Zhili was a Jurchen.

sentences.zh: 大父昔寶味也不干，登金進士第，金亡，歸太宗。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xibaoweiyebuyegan passed the Jin civil-service jinshi examination. When Jin fell he submitted to Emperor Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xibaoweiyebuyegan had passed the Jin jinshi examination; when the Jin fell he went over to Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 謁只里幼穎悟，能記誦，及長，以孝友聞。

translations.literal: Ye Zhili in youth was keen and perceptive, able to memorize and recite. When grown, he was known for filial piety and friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Zhili was bright as a boy and could memorize and recite with ease. As a man he was known for filial devotion and brotherly kindness.

sentences.zh: 事世祖潛邸，得備宿衛。

translations.literal: He served Kublai's hidden residence and obtained appointment in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: He served Kublai before his accession and was admitted to the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 中統初，命參議陝西行樞密院事，以商挺佐之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhongtong he was ordered to participate in deliberating Shaanxi Branch Bureau of Military Affairs affairs, with Shang Ting to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhongtong he was appointed to deliberate on Shaanxi military affairs, with Shang Ting as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 比行，入奏曰：「關陝要地，軍務非輕，阿脫仰剌國之元臣，陛下方委任之，伏慮臨時議論不協，必誤大計，儻有異同，臣請得以上聞。

translations.literal: Before departing he entered and memorialized: "Guan and Shaanxi are vital ground; military affairs are no light matter. Atai Yangla is a senior minister of the realm; Your Majesty is just now entrusting him. I fear that if discussions at the critical moment are not in accord, the great plan must be ruined. If there are differences, I ask to be allowed to report upward."
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving he memorialized at court: "Guan and Shaanxi are vital territory and the military burden is no light one. Atai Yangla is a senior minister of the realm whom Your Majesty has just entrusted with command. I fear discord at the decisive moment would wreck the larger plan. If differences arise, I ask permission to report directly to Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」帝可其奏，賜宴而遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his memorial, granted a banquet, and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved, gave him a farewell feast, and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改行省斷事官，復入宿衛。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to Branch Secretariat judicial officer and again entered palace guard service.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made a branch secretariat judicial officer and returned to palace guard duty.

sentences.zh: 李璮平，朝議選宿衛之士監漢軍，謁只里佩虎符，監軍於毗陽。

translations.literal: When Li Tan was pacified, the court deliberated on selecting palace guard soldiers to supervise Han armies. Ye Zhili wore the tiger tally and supervised troops at Piyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Tan's rebellion was crushed, the court chose palace guards to oversee Han armies. Ye Zhili took the tiger tally and supervised troops at Piyang.

sentences.zh: 至元七年，命為監戰，以所領諸軍圍襄陽，築一字堡以張軍勢，一時名將唆都、劉國傑、李庭等皆隸麾下。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan he was ordered to be battle supervisor; with the various armies he led he besieged Xiangyang, building linear fortresses to display military power. At one time famed generals Suodu, Liu Guojie, Li Ting, and others were all under his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan he was appointed battle supervisor, besieged Xiangyang with his command, and built chained forts to project strength. The famous generals Suodu, Liu Guojie, Li Ting, and others all served under him.

sentences.zh: 攻樊城，率其軍先登，破之，所受賞賜，悉分將士。

translations.literal: Attacking Fancheng he led his army first to mount and broke it. The rewards he received he entirely divided among officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: At the assault on Fancheng he was first over the wall with his men and took the city. He gave away every reward he received to his officers and men.

sentences.zh: 十一年，從丞相伯顏次郢州，將數騎而出，與宋兵遇，有部卒墮馬，為其所得，謁只里單騎橫戈，直入其軍，取之以還，因殺獲四人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he followed Chief Councilor Bayan, halting at Yingzhou. Leading several horsemen he went out and encountered Song troops. One of his troopers fell from his horse and was seized by them. Ye Zhili alone rode, spear crosswise, straight into their army, retrieved him and returned, and thereby killed and captured four men.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he followed Chief Councilor Bayan to Yingzhou. Riding out with a few horsemen he ran into Song troops. One of his men was unhorsed and captured. Ye Zhili charged in alone, spear level, broke into their ranks, brought his man back, and killed or captured four more.

sentences.zh: 時糧儲不繼，諸將以為憂，謁只里乃西攻江陵龍灣堡，取其粟萬石，衆賴以濟。

translations.literal: At that time grain stores did not continue; the generals were troubled. Ye Zhili then attacked west Jiangling's Longwan Fort, took ten thousand shi of their grain, and the host relied on this to get through.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies were running short and the generals were worried. Ye Zhili attacked Longwan Fort near Jiangling, seized ten thousand shi of grain, and the army was saved.

sentences.zh: 元兵東下，宋將夏貴迎戰於陽邏洑，伯顏未至，衆欲少俟之，謁只里曰：「兵貴神速，機不可失，宜及其未定而擊之。

translations.literal: As Yuan troops moved east, Song general Xia Gui met them in battle at Yangluofu. Bayan had not yet arrived; the crowd wished to wait briefly for him. Ye Zhili said: "In war speed is prized; opportunity cannot be lost — one ought to strike them before they are settled."
translations.idiomatic: As the Yuan army marched east, Song General Xia Gui met them at Yangluofu. Bayan had not yet arrived and the others wanted to wait. Ye Zhili said: "Speed is everything in war — the chance will not wait. We should hit them before they are set."

sentences.zh: 」遂直前衝貴軍，獲戰船百餘，貴敗走。

translations.literal: He then drove straight forward and charged Gui's army, seized more than a hundred battle boats; Gui was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He charged straight at Xia Gui's line, captured more than a hundred warships, and drove Gui off in defeat.

sentences.zh: 伯顏上其功，加定遠大將軍。

translations.literal: Bayan reported his merit; he was promoted to General for Settling the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan reported his exploit and he was promoted to General for Settling the Distance.

sentences.zh: 十二年，攻常州，謁只里造雲梯繩橋以登，遂克之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year they attacked Changzhou. Ye Zhili built cloud ladders and rope bridges to scale the walls and thereupon took the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, attacking Changzhou, Ye Zhili built siege ladders and rope bridges to scale the walls and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 奉省檄徇安吉諸州，皆下。

translations.literal: By provincial order he subdued Anji and other prefectures; all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: By provincial order he brought Anji and the surrounding prefectures to submission.

sentences.zh: 十三年，宋降，伯顏命謁只里監守其宮，號令嚴肅，秋毫無犯。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Song surrendered. Bayan ordered Ye Zhili to guard the palace; his commands were strict and disciplined, and not the slightest thing was taken in violation.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, when Song surrendered, Bayan ordered Ye Zhili to guard the palace. His discipline was severe and not the slightest thing was disturbed.

sentences.zh: 入朝，錄功，遷昭勇大將軍。

translations.literal: He came to court; his merit was recorded and he was transferred to General of Manifest Valor.
translations.idiomatic: He came to court, his achievements were recorded, and he was promoted to General of Manifest Valor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜鎮國上將軍、浙東宣慰使，鎮守紹興。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed General Who Stabilizes the Realm and Pacification and Comfort Commissioner of eastern Zhe, garrisoning Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed General Who Stabilizes the Realm and Pacification Commissioner of eastern Zhe, with his base at Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 十九年卒，年四十二。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died at age forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the nineteenth year at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 子亦老溫，襲為萬戶，累遷江東廉訪使；

translations.literal: His son Yilaowen inherited as ten-thousand-household and was repeatedly promoted to censor of Jiangdong;
translations.idiomatic: His son Yilaowen inherited the ten-thousand-household post and rose to censor of Jiangdong;

sentences.zh: 脫脫，淮東宣慰使。

translations.literal: Tuotuo was Pacification and Comfort Commissioner of Huai East.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo served as Pacification Commissioner of Huai East.

sentences.zh: 鄭溫，真定靈壽人。

translations.literal: Zheng Wen was a man of Lingshou in Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Wen was a native of Lingshou in Zhending.

sentences.zh: 初從中書粘合南合南征，有功，為合必赤千戶。

translations.literal: At first he followed Secretariat Chancellor Nahananhe on the southern campaign, won merit, and became a Qibichi thousand-household.
translations.idiomatic: He first followed Chancellor Nahananhe on the southern campaign, distinguished himself, and became a Qibichi thousand-household.

sentences.zh: 從丞相史天澤，為新軍萬戶鎮撫。

translations.literal: He followed Chancellor Shi Tianze and served as commander-in-chief of the new army.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Chancellor Shi Tianze as commander-in-chief of the new army.

sentences.zh: 憲宗征西川，溫四月不解甲，天澤以溫見，具言其功，帝曰：「朕所親見也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong campaigned in western Sichuan, Wen did not remove his armor for four months. Tianze presented Wen and fully reported his achievements. The emperor said: "I have seen this with my own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Xianzong's western Sichuan campaign, Wen kept his armor on for four straight months. Tianze presented him and reported his achievements in full. The emperor said, "I have seen this myself.

sentences.zh: 」賜名也可拔都，賞以鞍勒。

translations.literal: He was granted the name Yekebadu and rewarded with saddle and bridle.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the name Yekebadu and rewarded with a saddle and bridle.

sentences.zh: 還至閬州，奉旨分軍守邏青居、釣魚等山，天澤命溫統四千人，警邏釣魚山。

translations.literal: When they returned to Langzhou, by imperial order troops were divided to guard the mountains of Qingju and Diaoyu and the rest. Tianze ordered Wen to command four thousand men to patrol and guard Diaoyu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to Langzhou, by imperial order troops were posted to guard Qingju, Diaoyu, and other heights. Tianze ordered Wen to command four thousand men to guard Diaoyu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 至元六年，進懷遠大將軍、右衛副都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan he was advanced to General of Cherished Distance and deputy commander of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan he was promoted to General of Cherished Distance and deputy commander of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 九年，詔溫統蒙古、漢人、女真、高麗諸部軍萬人，渡海征耽羅，平之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year an edict ordered Wen to command ten thousand troops of Mongol, Han, Jurchen, and Goryeo divisions, cross the sea to campaign against Tamna, and pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year an edict ordered Wen to lead ten thousand Mongol, Han, Jurchen, and Goryeo troops across the sea against Tamna and pacify the island.

sentences.zh: 十二年，陞右衛親軍都指揮使，率三衛軍萬人，從攻岳州、江陵、沙市、潭州，皆有功，平章阿里海涯賞銀十錠。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to commander of the Right Guard and led ten thousand men of the three guards in attacks on Yuezhou, Jiangling, Shashi, and Tanzhou, winning merit in each. Chief Councilor Alihaiya rewarded him with ten ingots of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was made commander of the Right Guard and led ten thousand men of the three guards in the assaults on Yuezhou, Jiangling, Shashi, and Tanzhou, distinguishing himself in each. Chief Councilor Alihaiya rewarded him with ten ingots of silver.

sentences.zh: 十四年，入朝，遷昭勇大將軍、樞密院判官。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he came to court and was transferred to General of Manifest Valor and vice minister of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he came to court and was made General of Manifest Valor and vice minister of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 十八年，改輔國上將軍、江淮行省參知政事。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was changed to Assistant-to-the-State General and associate administrator of the Jiang-Huai Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was made Assistant-to-the-State General and associate administrator of the Jiang-Huai Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 杭民饑，出米二十萬石糶之。

translations.literal: The people of Hangzhou were starving; he released two hundred thousand shi of grain for sale at reduced price.
translations.idiomatic: When Hangzhou faced famine, he released two hundred thousand shi of grain for sale at reduced price.

sentences.zh: 俄賜以常州官田三十頃。

translations.literal: Shortly he was granted thirty qing of official fields at Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was granted thirty qing of official land at Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，召還。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，陞江浙左丞，命以新附漢軍萬五千，於淮安雲山白水塘立屯田。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was promoted to left vice-censor of Jiang-Zhe and ordered to establish agricultural colonies at Yunshan Baishuitang in Huai'an with fifteen thousand newly submitted Han troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was promoted to left vice-censor of Jiang-Zhe and ordered to establish agricultural colonies at Yunshan Baishuitang in Huai'an with fifteen thousand newly submitted Han troops.

sentences.zh: 二十八年卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died at age eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-eighth year at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 子欽，利用監丞；

translations.literal: His son Qin was supervisor of the Utilization Office;
translations.idiomatic: His son Qin was supervisor of the Utilization Office;

sentences.zh: 釭，榷茶都運使；

translations.literal: Gang was director-general of the tea monopoly;
translations.idiomatic: Gang was director-general of the tea monopoly;

sentences.zh: 銓，右衛親軍千戶；

translations.literal: Quan was thousand-household of the Right Guard;
translations.idiomatic: Quan was thousand-household of the Right Guard;

sentences.zh: 鏞，袁州路判官。

translations.literal: Yong was judge of Yuanzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Yong served as judge of Yuanzhou Circuit.
